Lamar Jackson suffered a thumb injury in Week 8 against the Buffalo Bills and is on injured reserve, shifting the line for this game from Ravens -3 (the lookahead) to Jaguars -9.5. That move also comes after backup Tyler Huntley (turf toe) was ruled out for this game and third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano is dealing with an ankle injury. So, the Ravens are in a brutal spot as they look to get back over .500 (Baltimore is 4-4 this season) against the top team in the AFC South. Jacksonville is in a great spot to win the AFC South for the second season in a row, as no other team in the division has more than two wins in 2026. The Jags blew out the Indianapolis Colts – 42-7 – in Week 8, and they’re one of the best defenses in the league, ranking third in EPA/Play and eighth in success rate. Liam Coen’s team is a deserved favorite in this matchup, which could be a tough one to bet on with all the Baltimore injuries. Still, the SI Betting team has curated some picks for Week 9’s Thursday Night showdown, including player props for Lawrence and Derrick Henry. Here’s a breakdown of some of our favorite bets for the action to kick off the final week of the first half of the 2026 season. Best NFL Picks and Predictions for Jaguars vs. Ravens Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Jacksonville Jaguars -8.5 (-115) vs. Baltimore Ravens – Iain MacMillan Bhayshul Tuten Anytime TD (+115) – Peter Dewey Trevor Lawrence UNDER 31.5 Pass Attempts (-118) – Peter Dewey Derrick Henry UNDER 70.5 Rushing Yards (-109) – Peter Dewey All season long, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan shares his favorite bet for every game in his Road to 272 column , and he’s taking the Jaguars to cover on the road with Baltimore dealing with some major quarterback issues: The Baltimore Ravens don't have a quarterback, which is obviously a pretty important aspect of being competitive in an NFL game. Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley are likely out for the game, and their third-string quarterback, Joe Fagnano, is also questionable due to an injury. If he can't go, the Ravens are going to be starting a quarterback who's not on their roster as of me writing this article on Monday night. That leaves the Ravens' only plan of attack being running the football. Unfortunately, they now have to face a Jaguars defense that ranks second in opponent rush EPA and seventh in opponent rush success rate, while giving up fewer yards per carry than any other defense in the league (3.4). I could maybe be convinced to take the points with the Ravens if they had an elite defense, but they're completely average on that side of the ball. Jaguars second-year running back Bhayshul Tuten has played a major role on offense this season, appearing in 55.3 percent of the team’s snaps while registering at least 12 carries in every game. Tuten also has six straight games with two or more receptions, finding the end zone three times through the air and four times overall in his last two games. Chris Rodriguez is also going to factor into the Jacksonville attack, but I’m buying Tuten at +115 to find the end zone on Thursday. While Baltimore is allowing just 3.8 yards per carry this season, it’s already allowed 10 rushing scores. This could be a run-heavy game script for the Jags since they’re nearly favored by double digits, and Tuten has six total scores in seven games in 2026. He should continue to see a ton of work as the Jaguars look to run away with the AFC South. A former No. 1 overall pick, Lawrence is in the MVP conversation this season, but he hasn’t been asked to throw the ball a ton with this Jaguars offense humming on the ground in 2026. Lawrence is averaging under 29 pass attempts per game in 2026, and he threw the ball just 14 times in a 42-7 win over Indianapolis in Week 8. Overall, the star quarterback has just two games (Weeks 5 and 6) where he even attempted 30 passes. So, with the Jaguars heavily favored on a short week, I expect a lighter workload for Lawrence against a Ravens team that has lost three straight and is staring down a lost season with Jackson sidelined. If this game turns into a blowout like the Colts matchup did, Lawrence may not even attempt 25 passes for the fourth time in eight games. This season, Derrick Henry has just four games with over 70 rushing yards, and he’s coming off three straight down performances with 58, 45 and 53 rushing yards, allowing just 3.5 yards per carry during that stretch. The Jaguars are going to stack the box against Henry with all of Baltimore’s quarterback issues, and Jacksonville held Jonathan Taylor to under 30 rushing yards in a blowout in Week 8. The game script isn’t going to be favorable for Henry, and he only saw 11 rushes in Week 8. Jacksonville ranks No. 1 in the NFL in EPA/Rush, allowing the fewest yards per carry (3.4) and total rushing yards (542) in the league this season. picks.blurb: Prediction For Jaguars' Huge Thursday Night Clash With the Baltimore Ravens - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football MNF: Bills-Vikings live updates Week 10 Waiver Wire Jaguars' blockbuster deal Giannis left 'speechless' CFP doubling in size (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect) Jason Klingensmith · Roundtable Sports Thu, November 5, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads When the NFL schedule was released in May, the Week 9 Thursday Night Football clash between the Jacksonville Jaguars and Baltimore Ravens looked like one of the season's marquee games. It was expected to be a matchup featuring two AFC heavyweights, one that would carry significant playoff implications. The Jaguars have held up their end of the bargain, racing out to a 5-2 record and looking like one of the NFL's elite teams. The Ravens, on the other hand, have fallen short of expectations. They are only 4-4 and in last place in the AFC North. Two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson returned in Week 8 from a three-game absence due to a high-ankle sprain, only to suffer a serious thumb injury on the first snap against the Buffalo Bills . Jackson's newest injury requires surgery and is expected to sideline him for the rest of the season , likely ending Baltimore's chances of reaching the Super Bowl. Jackson's backup, Tyler Huntley, also went down with a season-ending turf toe injury after replacing Jackson against Buffalo. Now Baltimore must turn to undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano, who will be making his first NFL start against a strong Jacksonville defense. Fagnano was also injured in the Bills' game, but has worked hard to play on Thursday night. On Wednesday, the Ravens traded for former Arizona Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett, who was just demoted to third-string after starting the team's first eight games. Brissett won't be ready to play against Jacksonville, leaving the offense in Fagnano's hands. The Jaguars must overcome their own injury issues to walk out of Baltimore with their sixth victory of the season. Jacksonville also suffered a pair of season-ending injuries in its Week 8 42-7 thrashing of the Indianapolis Colts. Run-stuffing defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton will miss the rest of the year after tearing his quad. Starting safety Eric Murray joined Hamilton on injured reserve with an elbow injury. Running back Bhayshul Tuten, who is having a phenomenal season, is a game-time decision after not practicing all week with ankle and foot injuries. Star edge rusher Travon Walker is questionable with a rib ailment, though he got in limited practices on Tuesday and Wednesday. Without Jackson, Baltimore will likely lean on star running back Derrick Henry to help take the pressure off Fagnano. Henry remains one of the NFL's premier RBs. As long as he is on the field, the Ravens remain a dangerous team. Stopping Henry is number one of my five keys to a Jaguars' victory . Jacksonville has the league's top run defense, but it will be hard to overcome the loss of Hamilton. Expect the Jaguars to load the box to keep Henry contained and force Baltimore's crippled passing attack to beat them. Offensively, Jacksonville's potent attack should have success against a Ravens defense that allows over 25 points per game. QB Trevor Lawrence is playing at an MVP level and could have a big night against Baltimore's suspect pass defense. For the second game in a row, the Jaguars are playing a team that will be at much less than full strength. Last week, the Colts got an early start on their rebuild by trading stars Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner before playing Jacksonville. Now the Jaguars get to play a Ravens team missing its superstar QB and his primary backup. An undrafted rookie QB making his first NFL start against a terrific team like Jacksonville is a nightmare scenario for the Ravens. In the days of Ray Lewis, Ed Reed, and Terrell Suggs, Baltimore's defense could dominate a game without needing help from the offense. Those days are long gone. The Jaguars dominate and improve to 6-2. Prediction: Jaguars 34, Ravens 10

On the positive side, the Ravens will be playing in front of their home crowd. However, they are going to be playing without superstar quarterback Lamar Jackson and backup signal caller Tyler Huntley. Getting the start will be undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano. He came into the game last week against the Buffalo Bills and made his NFL debut, completing 10 of his 21 pass attempts for 91 yards, no touchdowns, and an interception. Hailing from Boston College, the 6-foot-3 and 225-pound quarterback threw for 3,448 yards, 28 touchdowns, and just one interception in 2025 with the Huskies. He completed 69 percent of his passes that year and chipped in with 131 yards and three touchdowns on the ground. Behind Fagnano, the team will have Kedon Slovis as the primary backup. He was signed off of the Green Bay Packers' practice squad this week. Baltimore has made the move to acquire Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals, but that trade will not finalize until later in the week. He won't be eligible to play against the Jaguars. Just hours before the game against Jacksonville kicks off, the Ravens have been slammed with a horrific prediction. Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio isn't giving Baltimore any chance to knock off the 5-2 Jaguars. He is predicting that the Ravens will be defeated by a final score of 27-13. At the end of the day, Baltimore has a lot of adversity to overcome. Sometimes, teams find the best of themselves in these moments. But, there is no question that the Ravens are facing an uphill battle against one of the top contenders in the AFC. Coming into this week's game, Baltimore has lost three straight games. Following their impressive 4-1 start, the Ravens are just 4-4 at this point in time. Obviously, the team's playoff hopes are very much in danger. Baltimore's hopes of winning a Super Bowl seem all but over. No one can fully count the Ravens out, but things are looking bleak. A win over Jacksonville would be a huge step towards getting back on track. On the other hand, a fourth straight loss would put Baltimore in a very difficult situation. Kickoff tonight is scheduled for 8:15 p.m. ET. Fans will be able to watch the game on Prime Video.

Their only real fix is swinging a trade for a starting-caliber replacement before the deadline hits. Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Moro Ojomo is floated as a top target for the Jaguars, although they will have to pay a premium for him. away.headline: Jaguars-Ravens Injury Report: Why Recent History Doesn't Bode Well for Bhayshul Tuten
away.blurb: The Jaguars released their final injury report for Thursday's Week 9 battle with the Baltimore Ravens, and it featured two big names as questionable: running back Bhayshul Tuten and defensive end Travon Walker. There is understandable concern for both, with Walker limited in practice on Tuesday and Wednesday after sustaining a rib injury in last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts. But recent history under this Jaguars regime suggests Walker has at least a chance to play. It does not say the same about Tuten. Simply put, the Jaguars will more than likely need Chris Rodriguez Jr. to step into a starting role on Thursday based on how they have handled past injury situations. Tuten did not practice on Tuesday or Wednesday, despite Jaguars head coach Liam Coen indicating in his pre-practice press conference that Tuten would have some sort of practice activity. Instead, Tuten was a DNP for the second day in a row, which has resulted in a missed game each time during the Coen era. This is the 25th game where the Jaguars are led by Coen and his staff. In the previous 24 final injury reports, the Jaguars have had 27 instances where a player did not practice during the week. In all 27 of those instances, the player missed the game that week. The key difference here is that Tuten is at least listed as questionable. All 27 previous instances of players missing practice led to them being outright ruled out, which of course has not been the case with Tuten. Coen has already tabbed Tuten as a game-time decision, something he has done two other times this year: in Week 1 with Cole Van Lanen and LeQuint Allen, who were each listed as questionable but played. The difference is that Van Lanen and Allen at least practiced that week. If this was a full week and not a Thursday Night Game, which the Jaguars have not played under Coen before, perhaps things would be different. But for now, most signs point toward Tuten not being available just simply based on the Jaguars' history under Coen. Perhaps one key that could answer the Tuten question is how Coen approached Van Lanen's status in Week 1. Van Lanen was coming off a serious knee injury that had kept him out of the entirety of training camp, though he returned in time to be limited in practice in Week 1. But a few weeks before then, here is what Coen had to say. home.headline: Lamar Jackson told Ravens he’s coming back this season, report says
home.blurb: Injured quarterback Lamar Jackson told teammates that he plans to return later this season, the NFL Network reported Sunday, citing anonymous sources. NFL Network reported that Jackson is undergoing surgery to repair a fractured and dislocated thumb on his right hand. Jackson’s injury typically takes at least six weeks to recover from, though it could take up to nine weeks, the report said. That would line up with a potential return during the Ravens’ four straight AFC North matchups to end the regular season, beginning Dec. 20 at the Pittsburgh Steelers. Perhaps the Ravens still have hope. “Just stay alive” was the paraphrase of Jackson’s message that he delivered within 24 hours of suffering a significant thumb injury on his throwing hand against Buffalo, the report said. After starting 4-1 with Jackson under center, Baltimore has slipped to 4-5 and last place in the AFC North, facing long odds to make the postseason. Jackson suffered the thumb injury on the offense’s first play of his first game back from an ankle injury in a 36-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills on Nov. 1. He and backup Tyler “Snoop” Huntley, who suffered a season-ending turf toe injury against Buffalo, were placed on injured reserve before Thursday night’s 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars , meaning they will miss at least four games. Jackson has not spoken to reporters since the injury, and coach Jesse Minter has declined to share details about it or Jackson’s potential recovery timeline. “I’m not going to speak on that,” Minter said when asked about Jackson on Thursday night. The Ravens have made plans to move forward without their two-time NFL Most Valuable Player this season, acquiring quarterback Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals last week. Though neither side disclosed the terms, Baltimore is reportedly sending Arizona a 2027 fourth-round draft pick and a 2028 seventh-round pick in exchange for the 33-year-old veteran and a 2027 fifth-round selection, ESPN reported. Brissett has started 73 of 109 games and completed 62.1% of his passes with 86 touchdowns and 39 interceptions. He also has 17 career rushing touchdowns. He is 23-50 as a starter. The move came about 12 hours after Baltimore’s embarrassing loss to the Jaguars at M&T Bank Stadium, where undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano made his first NFL start and struggled mightily with a heavily bandaged right ankle. He completed 10 of 18 passes for just 60 yards and was intercepted twice. Baltimore Ravens tell Derrick Henry they're not trading him ahead of NFL deadline - The Mirror US Skip to main content The Mirror US - News, Sports, Celebrities and Showbiz News The Ravens reportedly assured Derrick Henry he won't be traded, even as Lamar Jackson's injury and a losing streak have Baltimore at the bottom of the AFC North race Baltimore Ravens star running back Derrick Henry has watched his team's offense collapse amid major injuries under first-year head coach Jesse Minter, but the team has assured fans it won't trade the former Offensive Player of the Year before the deadline. The Ravens won't trade Henry before Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET NFL deadline despite falling to last in the AFC North. The decision follows a 33-10 defeat to Jacksonville that left the Ravens at 4-5 and searching for answers without Lamar Jackson . Henry hasn’t begged for a lifeline or tried to bail on a season gone sideways. He’s made it clear he’d rather attempt to bring Baltimore back to relevance than walk away from a battered roster that barely resembles the contender he signed up for in 2024. "I have not mentioned me going anywhere else," Henry said after Thursday's 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. The loss marked four straight defeats, and the Ravens haven't gone five straight without a win since 2007. "I'm saying, 'Let's go back to work. Let's try to get better and turn this thing around,'" he continued. When asked how the Ravens plan to turn things around, Henry shook his head and said, "We have to." "It’s the only thing we can do. Go back to work and try to get it going." In each of Baltimore's last three losses, the team gave up 30 points. Content cannot be displayed without consent ESPN's Adam Schefter reported on Saturday that the team has no plans to move him. Baltimore's quarterback and secondary issues initially led Ravens fans to think their star runner would leave. Henry has 689 rushing yards and eight touchdowns through nine games, averaging 3.9 yards per carry. Those numbers pale in comparison to his first Baltimore season, when he piled up 1,921 yards at 5.9 per attempt, or his 1,595-yard follow-up in 2025. Everything changed when Jackson hurt his thumb after returning from an ankle sprain that cost three games. With the two-time MVP in the lineup, Henry averaged 93.5 yards and seven touchdowns in four games. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights The NFL returns to Spain for the second straight season with a matchup that features many of the league's top offensive stars Getty Images Following a week without an international game, the NFL heads back overseas in Week 9 when it sends the Atlanta Falcons and Cincinnati Bengals to Spain. The Bernabéu will play host to American football for the second time in as many years as two divisional contenders descend upon Madrid. The Bengals are in search of their first win away from American soil in franchise history after going 0-1-1 in their previous two opportunities (the most recent contest dating back to 2019), while the Falcons seek to improve to .500 in games abroad. Atlanta is 2-3 away from the United States and last season lost in Berlin. This contest pits one of the league's hottest teams against a squad that aims to reestablish positive momentum. Cincinnati rides a three-game win streak into the Madrid Game and scored no fewer than 31 points in any of those triumphs, albeit with two of the matchups coming against bottom-tier competition. Atlanta, on the other hand, lost in two of its last three outings and went scoreless in its most recent showing. Both sides are alive and well in their respective divisions, but the context between the two differs greatly. The Falcons are just a half game back of first place in the NFC South, which may be the weakest division in football with no teams at or above .500 through the season's first two months. The Bengals' position at half a game out of the AFC North lead is the superior standing considering three teams own winning records. Where to watch Falcons vs. Bengals live Date: Sunday, Nov. 8 | Time: 9:30 a.m. ET Location: Bernabéu (Madrid) TV: NFL Network, stream on fubo Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bengals -3, O/U 52.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook Falcons vs. Bengals key storylines Bijan Robinson and Drake London see bounce-back opportunity: It is no small feat to keep one of the NFL's top running back-wide receiver tandems in check, but how much credit do the Tampa Bay Buccaneers deserve for doing so in Week 8? With due respect to a formidable defense, the weather in that shutout might have had more to do with the Falcons going scoreless than anything else. A major one-week swing could be in store for this duo as it squares off against a Cincinnati unit that just allowed the Tennessee Titans to rack up 36 points. Robinson remains the league's rushing leader with 780 yards on the year, and London stands sixth in receiving yards at 624. If the Bengals could not keep the Titans in check, they will have their hands even more full with these two stars. Tee Higgins reaches new echelon: Higgins has long played second fiddle to Ja'Marr Chase in the otherworldly Bengals passing attack but is now on level ground with his superstar teammate. Both saw exactly 61 targets across their first seven games, and both grabbed 43 catches on those opportunities. But Higgins has been the far more efficient receiver of the two with 726 yards. That ranks second in the NFL, only to potential repeat Offensive Player of the Year winner Jaxon Smith-Njigba . This is the best version of Higgins the league has seen, and it is on pace for historic production . James Pearce Jr . to make season debut: The NFL reinstated Pearce after he served an eight-game suspension for a violation of the league's personal conduct policy, which makes him eligible to play for the first time this season in Week 9. Atlanta has been surprisingly disruptive on the defensive front without the second-year pass rusher, who faced felony charges this offseason following a domestic dispute but is on track to have those charges dropped. A unit that ranks sixth in quarterback pressure rate may climb even closer to the top of the leaderboard and perhaps improve its sack totals upon Pearce's insertion into the lineup, because he logged 10.5 sacks as a rookie despite starting only three games. Joe Burrow on MVP pace: Only two quarterbacks ( Josh Allen and Brock Purdy ) have shorter odds, via DraftKings Sportsbook, to win the NFL's top individual award. Burrow leads both of them in touchdowns with a league-best 20, and he is a mere 0.1 points away from the NFL lead in passer rating at 111.6. This is so far the most efficient season of Burrow's stellar career, which is a pleasant development of an offense that missed him dearly when he missed a combined 16 games over the last three seasons due to injuries. The Falcons kept Purdy in check when they upset him and the San Francisco 49ers two weeks ago, but Burrow presents an even greater challenge and has a healthier supporting cast than the one Purdy brought into the Week 7 contest. Falcons vs. Bengals prediction Fans of American football in Spain are in for a treat, because this game has all the makings of a shootout. There is not an offense in the NFL that is clicking quite like the Bengals over the last three weeks, and between Burrow, Chase, Higgins, London and Robinson, five of the biggest names in football will be in action in a star-studded battle. Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr . should bounce back from last week's dreadful 8-for-24 showing in the rain, so Atlanta ought to have enough juice to keep pace with a team that is averaging 36.3 points per game since Oct. 11. In a matchup where points will be aplenty, the team with the better defense holds the edge. It is not as though Atlanta is vastly superior on that side of the ball, but it is much more reliable and is about to insert one of its projected top producers into the lineup for the first time this season. away.headline: Injured Bengals Defender Good to Go Against Falcons as Team Announces Inactives
away.blurb: Johnson was listed as questionable on the injury report with an ankle/foot designation after suffering the injury in last week’s 43-36 overtime win against the Tennessee Titans. Safety Kyle Dugger was ruled out Friday with the quad injury that has forced him to miss three of the last four games. Cornerback DJ Turner II injured his foot last week against the Titans and was limited to start the week, but he did not appear on the injury report and is expected to start and play his full role. Cincinnati Bengals defensive end Cedric Johnson is active for today’s NFL International Game in Madrid against the Atlanta Falcons. The other inactives are offensive tackle Myles Hinton, center Connor Lew and defensive tackle Landon Robinson. The Bengals only need four inactives today because their roster is currently at 52. The Bengals arrived in Madrid on Wednesday and practiced Thursday and Friday to get back on a normal weekly schedule. "I think this is the best compromise we found to make sure that we can get acclimated by Friday, get a really good practice where we feel better, and then play our best on Sunday," head coach Zac Taylor said on Thursday. The Indianapolis Colts host the Dallas Cowboys in a chaotic non-conference Week 9 tilt at Lucas Oil Stadium, with a looming trade deadline and an active fire sale casting a massive shadow over the home sideline. Despite dropping three of their last four games—capped off by a back-breaking collapse against Arizona—the Cowboys head to Indy as 5.5-point road favorites. However, while the Colts are clearly looking toward the future, my top Cowboys vs. Colts predictions and NFL picks are equally hesitant to trust Dallas on the road, pointing toward defensive flaws and roster uncertainty to find value ahead of the 1 p.m. ET kickoff on FOX today. TOP Pick Cowboys vs Colts prediction today: Over 51.5 At this point in the season, it's pretty much Over or nothing in Dallas Cowboys games. This team is the perfect recipe for topping the total. The offense is a high-octane attack, striking for big gains and playing at one of the fastest paces in the land. Meanwhile, the defense is a bunch of rusty lawn chairs, making every opposing passer look like an All-Pro arm. Next in line for a Dallas "Glow Up" is Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones , who's running the risk of getting cut after a bad start to 2026. To his defense, Indianapolis has faced some very stingy stop units the past few games , taking on the likes of Jacksonville, Minnesota, and Pittsburgh — all Top 10 in EPA allowed — with each of those meetings coming on the road. Jones and this offense are back home for just the second time in six weeks and face a Cowboys secondary near the bottom of almost every pass defense metric. And as bad as Dallas is at defending downfield, it's equally as stinky stopping the run. The Colts' defense is just as rotten. Indianapolis is 27th in defensive DVOA at FTN and has allowed the third most yards per play to foes entering Week 9 (5.9). away.headline: Cowboys’ Jerry Jones Makes Clear NFL Trade Deadline Statement Amid Injuries
away.blurb: The Dallas Cowboys head into Sunday’s Week 9 game against the Colts in decidedly rough shape on both sides of the ball, with star receiver George Pickens and star cornerback Joey Porter Jr. both out, as well as starting linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, who had been playing better before injuries again caught up to him. The combination of those injuries and the looming NFL trade deadline has raised questions, again, about what Dallas might do in the next 48 hours ahead of that looming deadline. On the Cowboys’ pregame show on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas, owner Jerry Jones was asked by Kristy Scales whether the team will take this new wave of injuries into consideration at the deadline on Tuesday. “No,” he said, “but that doesn’t mean something could not happen. Actually, you almost have to say that if anything could be considered or working, you really don’t know until—if it is substantive, for sure—you don’t have any idea that it could happen until you have a meeting of the minds and it is done. But for now, I don’t see it.” Cowboys’ Jerry Jones Already Made an NFL Trade Deadline Move Indeed, the Cowboys are in a position in which a move at the NFL trade deadline might not make much sense, even if there is a win in Indianapolis that pushes this bunch to 4-5. If this group can’t beat the fire sale Colts, then obviously, there’s no point in adding at the deadline. But even with a win, the Cowboys are down to just four draft picks in the 2027 draft, and there just is not much more capital this team can afford to give away. Jones, who added Quinnen Williams in a blockbuster trade at last year’s deadline, has said that the move for Porter should be viewed as this year’s big deadline acquisition. Like HEAVY's content? Be sure to follow us . This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Cowboys’ Jerry Jones Makes Clear NFL Trade Deadline Statement Amid Injuries appeared first on HEAVY .

away.headline: Cowboys Injury Roundup: 'Tough decisions' ahead as Ferguson, Locke, others get bad news
away.blurb: FRISCO, Texas — Roughly two weeks ago, the Dallas Cowboys were feeling great about their injury report as key players began to get healthy and return to the practice and playing field. In the blink of an eye, they're suddenly back to having a lengthy and growing list of injuries that will again cost them impact players going forward. PJ Locke missed time this season before returning and suffering a concussion in Week 8, clearing protocol ahead of the matchup against the Indianapolis Colts before suffering a second concussion in as many weeks and, this time, he will not return in only a week's time. On Monday, head coach Brian Schottenheimer and the Cowboys officially ruled Locke out of the looming contest against the San Francisco 49ers — a sign he will likely miss multiple games. It was a scary sight to see Locke lying motionless for several moments before being helped to the sideline and not being permitted to return at Lucas Oil Stadium. Turpin will join DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring/back), George Pickens (hamstring) and Joey Porter Jr. (ankle), those three were ruled out ahead of kickoff against the Colts, in the rehab group this week to determine if either of them can go against the 49ers. And with Ferguson down, the expectation is that Luke Schoonmaker will return from injury to help with the currently ailing tight end depth chart. And though Marist Liufau was activated from injured reserve last week, Malachi Lawrence recently joined Thompson on IR, leaving the Cowboys with only one IR-DTR (designated to return) spot this regular season, assuming Lawrence returns as expected. That means if Ferguson, Goodson and Locke are moved to IR, only one of them would be allowed to return unless the Cowboys make the playoffs. In pulling out a much-needed win in Indianapolis, the Cowboys seemingly took craziness to a whole new level. After challenging his defense to execute for a full 60 minutes, Quinnen Williams led by example with a dominant performance that helped the Cowboys finish strong and close out a crucial victory. Cowboys Injury Roundup: 'Tough decisions' ahead as Ferguson, Locke, others get bad news Skip to main content Primary nav NEWS Patrik Walker DallasCowboys.com Staff Writer On the offensive side of the ball, the team will be without tight end Jake Ferguson and Tyler Goodson for "multiple weeks", Schottenheimer added, both nursing knee injuries suffered against the Colts. Ferguson scored the first touchdown for the Cowboys in Indy on an athletic catch before a later hit ended his afternoon, and Goodson actually returned after suffering his injury, but tests after the game revealed a very concerning issue that has yet to be disclosed. Goodson finished with 77 rushing yards on 6.7 yards per carry in Week 9, ratcheting up his impact as both RB2 and a kick returner in the absence of KaVontae Turpin (ribs). away.headline: Cowboys injury report: Overshown’s latest setback, Pickens and Porter Jr. updates
away.blurb: But the Cowboys won't be going into this game fully staffed either. Earlier this week, fans learned that Malachi Lawrence would be out for several weeks with an ankle injury, but he's not the only one in danger of missing this weekend's contest. Let's check out the latest regarding DeMarvion Overshown, George Pickens, Joey Porter Jr., Caleb Downs and others. On Friday, Schotteheimer told 105.3 The Fan that they needed to "get him out there today and see how he does.” Overshown is questionable after being limited the last two days. It always seems to be something with him, unfortunately, so fans won't hold their breath for Overshown to be active. Pickens has been dealing with a multitude of injuries this year, it seems, which at least partially explains his downturn in production. He was limited in all three practices leading up to the Colts game, and he is also questionable for Sunday. Dallas knew Porter Jr. was not 100% upon his arrival, but he's been a mainstay on the injury report and a full-on question mark every week, it feels like. He was full on Wednesday but has been limited the last two days, which is a bit worrisome, but Porter Jr. is questionable for Week 9. Schottenheimer said before Friday's practice that he was "hopeful" to have both Pickens and Porter Jr. against Indianapolis. Fans will find out Sunday morning if that was just wishful thinking. After missing the last two-plus games, Dee Winters will return for Dallas. The Cowboys have not had a fully healthy linebacker corps for an entire game this season, and if Overshown misses Sunday, it will remain that way. But for the time being, he is at least insurance if Overshown is out. Jake Ferguson improved from a non-participant on Wednesday and Thursday to being limited on Friday. It remains to be seen if he can play through his ankle injury, but he is officially questionable. Of course, Malachi Lawrence is out with the aforementioned ankle injury, and Kavontae Turpin will miss his third straight game with an injury to his ribs. Jonathan Bullard and Marist Liufau have not been activated to the 53-man roster, but they both practiced in full all week. Officially, they are questionable as the Cowboys mull over their roster math equations. Rapid fire: Luke Schoonmaker is questionable. Tyler Smith and Kenny Clark are good to go. The Dallas Cowboys' season already feels like it is on the ropes in Week 9 as they travel to take on one of the only teams in the NFL that are spiraling worse than they are: the Indianapolis Colts. And this is a get-right game if I've ever seen one, or if that even matters for Brian Schottenheimer's team. Indianapolis has already sold off great veterans like Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, and word on the street is that Josh Downs and Jonathan Taylor, and maybe more, could be next. The vibes are certainly low in the Colts' locker room, and some "business decisions" could be made on Sunday. Dallas Cowboys injury update before Week 9 game vs. Indianapolis Colts

away.blurb: Sunday’s matchup at Lucas Oil Stadium brings together two teams badly in need of a reset, as the Dallas Cowboys (3-5) visit the Indianapolis Colts (2-6) at 1 p.m. ET. Dallas is coming off a crushing 33-30 overtime loss to Arizona in which it led 24-10 early in the fourth quarter and 30-24 in the final minute, only for Gardner Minshew to lead an 80-yard game-tying touchdown drive before Chad Ryland won it with a 42-yard field goal in overtime. Dak Prescott completed 19 of 29 passes for 195 yards and a touchdown and added a five-yard rushing score, but Dallas managed only 261 total yards and went three-and-out on its lone overtime possession. The loss dropped the Cowboys to 3-5 and magnified a season-long problem: the defense. Dallas is allowing 26.6 points and 385.4 yards per game. The most recent meeting between these teams produced one of the wildest quarters in Cowboys’ history. On December 4, 2022, Indianapolis trailed 21-19 entering the fourth quarter in Arlington before Dallas erupted for 33 unanswered points to win 54-19. Prescott threw three touchdown passes, Tony Pollard ran for 91 yards and two scores, and the Cowboys forced five turnovers, including Malik Hooker’s 38-yard fumble-return touchdown against his former team. The recent series has otherwise gone back and forth: Indianapolis shut out Dallas 23-0 in 2018, Dallas won 42-7 in 2014, the Cowboys earned a 38-35 overtime victory in 2010, and Dallas won 21-14 in 2006. away.blurb: Jonathan Taylor, Keenan Allen, and Charvarius Ward all returned to full participation after sitting out Wednesday on rest days. Indianapolis could also receive reinforcements at a couple of positions. Linebacker Bryce Boettcher and wide receiver Anthony Gould have both logged consecutive full practices after missing the previous two games. The Cowboys could receive some reinforcements at linebacker, with Dee Winters progressing from limited participation Wednesday to a full practice Thursday. Winters' potential return would be particularly helpful with DeMarvion Overshown being limited with hamstring and back issues. Meanwhile, Marist Liufau has also returned to full participation as he works through his 21-day return-to-practice window, potentially giving Dallas another option at linebacker. The secondary is another area worth monitoring. Caleb Downs and P.J. Locke both progressed from not participating Wednesday to limited participation Thursday while dealing with concussions, an encouraging sign for Dallas. Both players must complete the NFL's concussion return-to-participation protocol. Their return to practice is encouraging, but neither is guaranteed to be available Sunday. Joey Porter Jr. also went from a full participant on Wednesday to limited on Thursday with an ankle injury. With multiple defensive backs dealing with injuries, Dallas could be facing some significant depth concerns against Indianapolis. At tight end, Jake Ferguson has missed the first two practices of the week with an ankle injury, leaving his availability for Sunday in question. Luke Schoonmaker has been limited in consecutive practices while dealing with a groin injury, but his participation is an encouraging sign. home.headline: Colts' chances of fetching anything in return for QB Daniel Jones just went up in flames following report from NFL insider
home.source: A to Z Sports on MSN
home.blurb: Part of that decision likely comes down to the fact that the Colts extended Jones during the offseason. Pelissero also laid out what that contract looks like going forward. The Vikings are the team that loses out Minnesota has a Monday Night Football game this week. If Carson Wentz goes out there and stinks up the joint, the Vikings will be staring at a serious problem. Kyler Murray has been bad and is now injured, which leaves Minnesota with very few answers under center. For Colts fans, that means the rest of the season will play out with Jones as their starting quarterback. Whether that’s a comfort or a frustration probably depends on how you feel about the direction of this team. Either way, the Colts made their call, and Jones isn’t going anywhere. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. Read the full story here: Colts' chances of fetching anything in return for QB Daniel Jones just went up in flames following report from NFL insider Indianapolis shut down the Daniel Jones trade chatter, and one team that badly needed a quarterback answer just lost its best option. The Indianapolis Colts lost yet another game Sunday, this time to the Dallas Cowboys . With the NFL trade deadline arriving Tuesday, the rumor mill around the NFL is spinning. Who’s going? Who’s coming? Are the Colts about to sell off everybody? Quarterback Daniel Jones , running back Jonathan Taylor, wide receiver Josh Downs , and defensive tackle Grover Stewart have all come up in trade speculation. Well, we now know where Jones stands. Colts tell Daniel Jones he is staying put Tom Pelissero of The Ringer posted on that Indianapolis gave its quarterback a clear answer before the deadline: “The Colts informed quarterback Daniel Jones on Saturday They’re not trading him by Tuesday’s deadline. Teams called and the Colts listened, but they never had any intention of moving him despite speculation. Jones is staying in Indy.” The Colts' first-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft belongs to the Jets; the Colts' earliest pick projects at No. 39, according to the A to Z Sports NFL Playoff Predictor (updated Sun, Nov 8). “Daniel Jones is due $38 million in 2027 with only about $10.5 guaranteed for injury until March. That’s mid-tier quarterback money giving whoever the new GM is optionality as the rebuild begins.” That is the key detail here. Indianapolis isn’t locked into Jones long-term in a way that would hamstring a new front office. The flexibility is there, and there’s no need to rush a deal at the deadline when the decision can wait until the spring. Jones was asked about the trade rumors in his postgame interview, before Pelissero’s report surfaced. He made it clear where his loyalty lies. “I believe in Shane Steichen. I believe in what we’re doing. I love playing for Shane. So like I said, I hadn’t thought about it much. I’ve been so focused on Dallas and making sure I was ready.” That’s about as strong an endorsement of Colts head coach Shane Steichen as you’ll hear

According to a new report, general manager Brad Holmes and the Lions have already contacted the Indianapolis Colts about Charvarius Ward . With Detroit sitting at 6-2 following Sunday’s 19-9 victory over the Miami Dolphins, Holmes is facing an interesting decision. The Lions have won four consecutive games, but adding another experienced cornerback could provide valuable insurance for a team with legitimate Super Bowl aspirations. Detroit Lions Reportedly Contact Colts About Charvarius Ward “I’ve been told the Lions have already called on Ward,” Mike Payton wrote in his Nov. 9 report. “This one makes a ton of sense for Detroit; we’ll see if both sides can come to some sort of agreement.” That is an important development because Ward had previously been identified as one of several potential cornerback trade targets for Detroit . However, Payton’s latest report takes the conversation beyond hypothetical trade possibilities by indicating the Lions have actually made contact. Payton also emphasized that an inquiry does not necessarily mean negotiations are underway. Detroit could simply have been gathering information about Ward’s availability and potential asking price. Why Charvarius Ward Makes Sense for Detroit Ward would bring something the Lions could use down the stretch: an experienced outside cornerback who has handled significant responsibilities throughout his NFL career. The former Pro Bowler has played meaningful football with the Kansas City Chiefs and San Francisco 49ers, giving him experience against some of the league’s most dangerous offenses. His ability to play man coverage could also make him an intriguing fit in defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard’s system. Detroit has talented players in its secondary, but additional depth and veteran experience could become particularly valuable during a postseason run. The Lions have already been exploring potential upgrades at cornerback , and Ward represents a recognizable option with an established track record. He also remains under contract through the 2027 season, meaning Detroit could potentially retain him beyond this year. picks.blurb: Chiefs vs. Jets: NFL Week 9 Preview, Score Predictions Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI On the heels of consecutive losses to the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos, the Kansas City Chiefs are back at home and have a lighter game in the 12:00 p.m. local slot against the New York Jets. Just because New York doesn't have the makings of a playoff contender doesn't mean it can't give Kansas City a fight, though. The Chiefs know as well as any team that self-inflicted errors are the easiest way to hand a game over, so the hosts will have to put the pedal to the metal in order to secure a resounding triumph. With kickoff just hours away, will it be the Chiefs or Jets that emerge with a victory? The Kansas City Chiefs On SI crew makes its predictions for Week 9 of the regular season. Joshua Brisco: While there's only so much the Chiefs can truly prove against the 2-6 Jets, this is a game Kansas City simply has to win. A two-game losing streak to a pair of playoff teams is one thing. A home loss to a franchise that’s still a year away from even making the “in the hunt” playoff graphic? That would be disastrous. I’ll be watching to see if the Chiefs’ pass rush can wrangle Geno Smith, who is tied for the second-most sacks taken among quarterbacks this season, while hoping to see more from rookie R Mason Thomas in that effort. Will the Chiefs’ banged-up defense be able to hold down a lively group of weapons, even without Garrett Wilson, or will the KC offense need to score more than 24 points for the first time since before the bye week? I could see a bounce-back stat line for Kenneth Walker with another explosive play or two from the star running back. Jordan Foote: The Chiefs typically have at least one game a year they have no business losing and somehow just don't seem to show up for. While it's possible that this is the one, it absolutely cannot be the case. Coming off ugly losses to the Seahawks and Broncos (for different reasons), this is a squad that desperately needs to rebound in a hurry. Fortunately, the matchup is there in Week 9. The Jets' offense has had its shining moments, although it's virtually impossible to trust this version of Smith to go toe-to-toe with Patrick Mahomes if he's on his game. Add in that Kenneth Walker III may be due for another statement performance, and it's hard to see anything other than turnovers or penalties making this too close of a game, in my view. Tyler Brown: The Jets have been more competitive than their 2-6 record suggests, with five of their six losses coming by one score, and Geno Smith has been a pleasant surprise. They can be dangerous on offense, with wideouts Omar Cooper Jr. and Adonai Mitchell playing well lately and running back Breece Hall returning, even as Braelon Allen's rushed for 565 yards. This is also a real test for tackles Kahlil Benson and Jaylon Moore, who will face pass rushers David Bailey and Will McDonald IV. On the other hand, New York’s defense has been giving up production to opposing tight ends, which sets up Travis Kelce and Noah Gray well. Andy Reid can wear the Jets down with Kenneth Walker and, in a perfect world, let Patrick Mahomes work the secondary off that. Smith is also among the league’s worst at turning pressure into sacks, so a Chiefs pass rush that's been waiting for a game like this should hypothetically get home a few times. Neither team will run away, and the Jets will stay in it for a while. But Kansas City is the more talented team and needs the win more. The Chiefs have a stretch of must-win games ahead, and they find a way to handle this one. Published Nov 8, 2026 JORDAN FOOTE Jordan Foote covers the Kansas City Chiefs for Chiefs On SI. L'Jarius Sneed went on the injured reserve list , with No. 6 overall NFL Draft pick Mansoor Delane also sitting with a lingering shoulder issue. The latter injury remains a problem in Week 9, as head coach Andy Reid revealed on Friday that the star rookie would be inactive once again. In the same Friday media availability, Reid ruled defensive tackle Peter Woods out. Woods, who left Week 8's outing with a neck injury after just three snaps, didn't practice all week. Two other injury notes for the Chiefs pertain to supporting players on the depth chart. Special teams ace Nikko Remigio kicked off the week as a limited participant in practice but progressed to full participation in time to carry a questionable designation into Sunday. He's good to go. On defense, second-year tackle Omarr Norman-Lott was limited for another week and ruled out on Friday. Norman-Lott has one more week left in his 21-day evaluation window after being designated to return from the physically unable to perform list. He isn't listed among KC's inactives due to technically still not being on the active roster. On Saturday, the Chiefs activated defensive tackle Marcus Harris from the practice squad via standard elevation. New York Jets inactives vs. Kansas City Chiefs Harrison Phillips is active for #NYJvsKC WR Garrett Wilson WR Tim Patrick DB Nahshon Wright EDGE Joseph Ossai LB Trevin Wallace OL Kohl Levao OL Blake Freeland In advance of Sunday's game, the Jets ruled out multiple players. Wide receiver Garrett Wilson headlines the list, as he remains in concussion protocol and didn't practice all week. Elsewhere, players like linebacker Trevin Wallace (groin), defensive end Joseph Ossai (ankle) and cornerback Nahshon Wright (back) are also missing in action. Defensive tackle Harrison Phillips, who's been battling an ankle injury, was deemed questionable after not participating in Wednesday and Thursday's practices before getting a full workload on Friday. New York is letting him give it a go in Kansas City. Published Nov 8, 2026 JORDAN FOOTE Jordan Foote covers the Kansas City Chiefs for Chiefs On SI. Dodson · Athlon Sports Fri, November 6, 2026 at 11:16 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Kansas City Chiefs return home Sunday to face the New York Jets after dropping two straight games. Running back Kenneth Walker III has been bottled up in the defeats after leading the league in rushing through his first five games. The Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos limited K9 to a combined 105 rushing yards on 35 carries. Bold Prediction No. 1: Running Back Kenneth Walker Tops 100 Yards The Jets have allowed the seventh-most rushing yards to opposing running backs through eight weeks. Walker topped 100 yards on the ground in four of the first five games of the season. Even after averaging just 3.0 yards per carry the last two games, he's still second in the NFL with 5.5 yards per carry. Two weeks ago, the Jets allowed Miami Dolphins running back Ollie Gordon to rush for 103 yards on 25 carries . Walker is a clear upgrade from Gordon and will gash the Jets on the ground. The Chiefs' passing game has also had its issues. Tight end Travis Kelce has been managing an ankle injury, and they'll look to run the ball often. Bold Prediction No. 2: Chiefs Defense Records 2+ Sacks The Chiefs' pass rush has been much maligned, and it's for good reason. They're tied for last in the NFL with nine sacks on the season. Defensive tackle Chris Jones, who is one of their leading pass rushers, has just a half-sack on the season. Defensive end George Karlaftis reached the quarterback in Week 8 for his team-leading second sack of the season. The Jets are tied for second with 23 sacks allowed on the season. Quarterback Geno Smith has been sacked at least twice in the last seven games. Chiefs defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo is known for his relentless blitzing, and the Chiefs will get home two or more times.

picks.blurb: Previewing the New York Jets’ opposition: Kansas City Chiefs - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football MNF: Bills-Vikings live updates Week 10 Waiver Wire Jaguars' blockbuster deal Giannis left 'speechless' CFP doubling in size Previewing the New York Jets’ opposition: Kansas City Chiefs DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 1: Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs runs with the football and looks to pass during the third quarter against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on November 1, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. The Broncos defeated the Chiefs 28-24. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bent Double · SB Nation Sat, November 7, 2026 at 4:00 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Kansas City Chiefs have beaten the New York Jets in four of their five meetings since 2011, with the most recent being a controversial 23-20 win in 2023. That game saw Michael Carter II's game-clinching interception negated by a phantom penalty on Sauce Gardner and wasted one of the best performances of Zach Wilson's career. In this matchup, the Chiefs will be heavy favorites despite having lost two in a row following a 5-0 start. Let's break down the Chiefs' roster going position by position: The Jets have Patrick Mahomes to reckon with this week, and he's having a solid season as he's posting a quarterback rating of 99.7; his best since 2022. Mahomes has 12 touchdowns and four interceptions and is coming off a good game against the Broncos where he passed for 321 yards and three touchdowns with no interceptions. Behind Mahomes is a familiar face: Jets 2025 starter Justin Fields. Seventh round rookie Garrett Nussmeier is the number three. Offensive Line The Chiefs' interior line is the same as last year led by pro bowlers Creed Humphrey and Trey Smith at center and right guard respectively. Smith has a team-high five offensive penalties. Kingsley Suamataia completes the interior trio at left guard, although he's already been benched twice this year, including on Sunday where he was suddenly replaced before pre-game warmups by Mike Caliendo. That fuelled rumors that was was being disciplined by the coaching staff but Andy Reid denied this. Caliendo, who also started four games last year, has struggled in pass protection. Suamataia is expected to be back in the starting lineup for Sunday's game. The tackle positions have seen some changes as last year's starting right tackle, Jawaan Taylor, was released in March and the starting left tackle – 2025 first round pick Josh Simmons – is on injured reserve. Jaylon Moore, who started a handful of games last year, is currently starting at right tackle, while the left tackle is undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson, who is one of five undrafted rookies on the roster. Moore has given up a team-high three sacks, but Benson – while yet to surrender a sack – has given up the most pressure on the team. Moore missed week seven's game, so former New York Giant Joshua Ezeudu started at right tackle in that one. The other backups are center Hunter Nourzad and another undrafted rookie; tackle Diego Pounds. Running Backs The Chiefs' big offseason acquisition on offense was the reigning Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker. The move has been a resounding success as he rushed for 100 yards in four of his first five games as the Chiefs started 5-0. Since then, he's averaged just three yards per carry, though. Even so, he's just 10 yards off the league lead with 770 rushing yards. He has also caught 22 passes. There are two rookies backing up Walker – fifth round pick Emmett Johnson and the undrafted Jaydn Ott. Ott hasn't played yet, though. The Chiefs also have a fullback – Ben VanSumeren – on the roster. However, they will also use defensive tackle Khyiris Tonga in short yardage situations. He has even carried the ball twice. Pass catchers The Chiefs' top pass catching option has once again been tight end Travis Kelce, who has 410 receiving yards to lead the team. The leading pass catcher among the wide receivers is the speedy Xavier Worthy, who has 27 catches, albeit that he's only averaging 8.5 yards per catch. Despite some injury concerns and legal issues, Rashee Rice is now back in the lineup for the Chiefs. He has 20 catches in five games this year. Tyquan Thornton was also starting at wide receiver, but he's now on injured reserve. The backups are Jalen Royals, Andrew Armstrong, Nikko Remigio and fifth round rookie Cyrus Allen. Royals has seen the most action from this group. At tight end, Noah Gray is a solid contributor who gets plenty of playing time. Jake Briningstool and Jared Wiley round out this group. Defensive Line The Chiefs' defensive line is anchored by pro bowler Chris Jones, although he is having a down year statistically with just half a sack, one tackle for loss and three quarterback hits. He had 7.5, 12 and 25 last year. George Karlaftis, who had six sacks last year, has a team-high two sacks and also leads the team with 16 quarterback hits (just one less than the rest of the team combined) and six tackles for loss. Karlaftis also has a team-high with eight passes defensed. In fact, these all eight of these came in the last five games. Prior to that, he had 17 in his first 67 NFL games. Tonga is the other starter at defensive tackle with Felix Anudike-Uzomah the other starting defensive end. Kansas City has been operating a three-man rotation inside with first round rookie Peter Woods getting plenty of playing time. However, Woods has been ruled out with a neck injury so Bryson Eason may need to step up. Last year's second round pick Omarr Norman-Lott remains on the PUP list. The backups on the edge are second round rookie R Mason Thomas and Ashton Gillotte. Undrafted rookie Jack Pyburn is also on the roster. Nick Bolton remains in a full-time role with Drue Tranquill on the field most of the time. Last year, Bolton had 154 tackles and Tranquill added 103. They've been productive this year, too, with Bolton on 68 tackles and Tranquill on 53 tackles, including five tackles for loss. Jack Cochrane gets playing time in three-linebacker sets, while Jeffrey Bassa has seen limited action. Cooper McDonald has yet to play any defensive snaps, though. Defensive Backs The Chiefs suffered a loss a few weeks ago when their top cornerback L'Jairus Sneed was placed on injured reserve. Sneed was also the team's primary slot corner, so they've been using Christian Roland-Wallace in that role for the past few weeks. Nohl Williams and first round rookie Mansoor Delane are the current starters on the outside, although Kristian Fulton started in place of Delane on Sunday. Delane has a shoulder issue which is likely to limit him for the rest of the season but he was expected to return against the Jets. However, he has been ruled out, so Fulton will presumably start again. Melvin Smith and fourth round rookie Jadon Canady are also available to provide depth at cornerback. The starting safeties are Chamarri Conner, who had 117 tackles last season, and offseason signing Alohi Gilman. Jaden Hicks has also been getting playing time in three-safety sets. He also started the first three games with Conner out. Undrafted rookie safety Xavier Nwankpa has played five snaps so far this season. Special Teams Former pro bowl kicker Harrison Butker is having a rough year with six missed field goals already and Justin Tucker waiting in the wings on the practice squad in case he should falter again. Punter Matt Araiza is having his best year statistically in his third season with the Chiefs, though. Remigio is the team's return specialist, although Johnson ends up sharing the work on kickoff returns. Remigio, who is yet to achieve a 50-yard return as he is halfway through his third season, is officially listed as questionable. Bassa and Nwankpa are the team's most productive players in kick coverage this season, but last year they were led by McDonald and Cochrane. Canady and Nwankpa have been the primary gunners.

picks.blurb: Chiefs-Jets Week 9 game and score predictions from Arrowhead Pride - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football MNF: Bills-Vikings live updates Week 10 Waiver Wire Jaguars' blockbuster deal Giannis left 'speechless' CFP doubling in size Chiefs-Jets Week 9 game and score predictions from Arrowhead Pride (Photo by Jim McIsaac/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jared Sapp · SB Nation Fri, November 6, 2026 at 6:30 PM UTC · 9 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's time for the Arrowhead Pride staff to put their opinions to the test. Before the Kansas City Chiefs host the New York Jets — in their first matchup since 2023 — our writers predicted the final score and result. The 206 Jets are likely more focused on evaluating head coach Aaron Glenn — and the likelihood of having a trio of top ten selections in April's NFL Draft — than what happens the rest of the season. FanDuel Sportsbook currently lists the Chiefs as 9.5-point home favorites. Although the Jets lost to the Las Vegas Raiders 38-33 in Week 8, Gang Green did rack up 439 yards of offense, including 166 rushing yards. New York should not be considered a pushover opponent. We also want to know your score prediction! Vote in the poll on The Feed and share your score prediction ! Jared Sapp ( @TrumanChief ) It's been a hard fortnight to be a Chiefs fan. I am still of a mindset to see how this team looks at the end of the season, but losing any of the next three games would be catastrophic for the season. Earlier on, I was worried about the Chiefs sleeping on a team like the Jets. But after losing two straight games, I think the Chiefs will come out and play one of their best games of the season. The concern will remain of what happens against good teams, but I don't think you will see a play with their food performance at Arrowhead following a tough two-game road trip. Chiefs 31, Jets 17 Caleb James ( @CJScoobs ) After consecutive losses, the Chiefs badly need a win to get back on track. The Jets are a far cry from as bad as they have been in recent memory, but the Chiefs should win this game with minimal issues. The Jets are more talented offensively than they have been in some time, but running back Breece Hall has missed time this season with injury, and wide recieve Garret Wilson has shown up on the injury report. With a quality defense ranked near the top in several categories, the Chiefs will need to bring their A-game. Kansas City played a solid game offensively, but this week all eyes will be on the short-yardage and red zone situations where the team failed to convert in critical spots last week. Defensively, a turnaround game for the pass rush would be a big boost.I would continue to watch the emergence of Emmet Johnson alongside Kenneth Walker in creating a two-headed monster in the KC backfield. Chiefs 26, Jets 13 Mark Gunnels ( @MarkAGunnels ) I think the Chiefs are gonna handle the Jets at Arrowhead this week. If Garrett Wilson can't go, the Jets lose their best threat in the passing game, and Spags can load up on the run and make them beat Kansas City through the air. If Mahomes gets the Chiefs up two scores early, I don't see how the Jets keep up. I think this one gets out of hand in the second half. Maurice Elston ( @MrMauriceElston ) The Chiefs enter a three-game stretch that feels critical to keeping their AFC West title and No. 1 seed hopes within reach. After starting 5-0, Kansas City has dropped two straight, and the losing streak needs to stop Sunday against the Jets. New York has remained competitive, but this is a team the Chiefs should beat, especially back at Arrowhead in front of a crowd eager for something to celebrate. Garrett Wilson's uncertain availability could hurt the Jets, although Braelon Allen has proven their running game deserves respect regardless of Breece Hall's status. For Kansas City, getting Kenneth Walker III going starts with making defenses respect the passing game again. To me, his recent struggles go beyond the running back and offensive line. Tyquan Thornton's absence has taken away a deep threat, allowing defenses to crowd the line of scrimmage. The Chiefs must find ways to stretch the field without him, create room for Walker and get back to building off play-action. I expect Patrick Mahomes and Andy Reid to find those answers this week, with Kansas City settling down and delivering a convincing win. Chiefs 27, Jets 13 Matt Stagner ( @stagdsp ) The New York Jets come to town at a pretty good time for the Chiefs. Having lost the past two games, they'll be hungry to get back in the win column. Andy Reid has rightfully been blamed for the team's failures over the last couple of weeks, so I'd expect at least a "B" game plan on Sunday. He should let Kingsley come back as the left guard, and Rashee Rice is getting healthier— these two developments alone could get the offense moving enough to beat the Jets. But the Chiefs also have developing weapons in Emmett Johnson and Cyrus Allen. Both rookies should continue to see increased touches every week from here to the postseason (in my humble opinion). I'm of the opinion that the Chiefs are still in pretty good shape overall— the Denver loss hurt, but KC looked like the better squad. The Jets aren't as bad as their record either, so this won't be a cakewalk, but I expect the home crowd will have plenty to cheer about. Chiefs 28, Jets 13 Dakota Watson ( @D_Watson56 ) I hope the Chiefs are as angry as the fan base after that last game. Because they need to play angry, even against the Jets, if they're going to turn this season around. Now in a fight for the division, the Chiefs must take advantage of these next three games against what seems like inferior opponents. While I have serious concerns about this football team, I believe they get back in the win column this weekend. The offense should be able to get in a rhythm and right some of their wrongs from the past two weeks. And for the Jets, if Garrett Wilson can't go, then I think the Chiefs' defense should hold their own and focus on shutting down their running game. Chiefs win fairly comfortably in this one. Chiefs 28, Jets 17 Rocky Magana ( @RockyMagana ) It's been a rough couple of weeks. The Chiefs have lost back-to-back games. But they played well enough in Denver that they should have won that game. Some poor coaching decisions and a few mental lapses are all it takes in the NFL to lose to a division rival. That being said, this should be a get-right game for the Chiefs. The New York Jets are having a very Jets-like year and have struggled to move the ball and score points. They are also averaging 123.6 yards allowed per game on the ground. The Chiefs should plan on dealing a healthy dose of Kenneth Walker III and Emmett Johnson to them. This could be the perfect get-right game for Kansas City. Chiefs 24, Jets 10 Nate Christensen The Jets have been a better team this year. Their offense has dramatically improved with Geno Smith at quarterback and an impressive set of weapons. Braelon Allen has broken out at running back. Adonai Mitchell, Garrett Wilson, and Omar Cooper have formed a good trio. They have good young tight ends and two top-10 draft picks at tackle. Their offense can score and keep them in games The issue has been their defense, which is bad. They don't have a lot of talent, particularly in the secondary. I think the Chiefs should easily be able to throw the ball this week, and I expect Kenneth Walker to bounce back with a big game. Chiefs 34, Jets 23 Ron Kopp Jr. ( @RonOnChiefs ) Welcome to Game 1 of three that the Chiefs are fully expected to win, similar to the first five games of the season. The Jets are talented on offense and competitive on defense; they have too many recent first-round picks not to be, but there's nothing Aaron Glenn and company can do about Kansas City needing a confidence-building win after two straight losses. Look for the Chiefs' run game to come alive again and marry it to a passing attack that found answers against the Broncos last week until the final play. Whether the wide receivers are a big part of the game plan, I see Kansas City lighting up the scoreboard and putting this game out of reach in the second half. Chiefs 38, Jets 20 2026 Standings Nate Chrstensen Maurice Elston Dakota Watson Nate Christensen (17-13) stood alone among the AP panel in choosing the Broncos to win last week. Nate now moves into second place among our three 6-1 contributors. Based on error margins, Ron remains in first place. 56.6% of our readers likely felt good about their prediction of a close Chiefs' victory until the final moments of the contests. 22.3% did predict a close Broncos win. *To calculate a prediction's points of error, the differences between the prediction and the actual score in point spread, home team score, and away team score are added together. For example, a prediction calls for a 17-10 Chiefs win. They end up winning 16-10, so there were two points of error: the point spread was off by one point, the Kansas City score missed by one point, and the opponent's score was predicted correctly. But if the Chiefs lose the game 17-10, there were 28 points of error in the prediction: the point spread was off by 14 (the difference between +7 and -7), and both scores were off by 7.

away.headline: Kansas City Chiefs' first injury report for Week 9 vs. New York Jets sees top 2026 NFL Draft pick return to practice
away.source: A to Z Sports on MSN
away.blurb: Chiefs HC Andy Reid told reporters Wednesday that DT Peter Woods would not practice because of the stinger he suffered in Week 8’s loss to the Broncos . He was the only player who didn’t participate in practice, with CB Mansoor Delane (shoulder) returning in a limited capacity . DT Omarr Norman-Lott continues his ramp-up period after being designated to return to practice. He’s missed quite a bit of time with an ACL injury. As for the Jets, they’re also navigating a few injuries. They were without their biggest offensive star, WR Garrett Wilson, on Wednesday. KEY: DNP = Did not participate | LP = Limited participation | FP = Full participation | NIR = Not injury related We’ll see how Peter Woods progresses through the practice week, it wouldn’t be unreasonable for him to return to action with a limited practice on Thursday and a full practice on Friday. Andy Reid said on Monday that Mansoor Delane would have a chance to play this week. Limited practice puts him on track to return after missing Week 8’s game against the Broncos. Travis Kelce and Rashee Rice being limited is planned maintenance. The player to watch is WR Nikko Remigio. The hip injury is new, and Emmett Johnson has recently flashed his ability on special teams as a return specialist. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. Read the full story here: Kansas City Chiefs' first injury report for Week 9 vs. New York Jets sees top 2026 NFL Draft pick return to practice The Kansas City Chiefs’ first injury report ahead of Week 9 vs. the New York Jets has a few key players trending in a positive direction. The Kansas City Chiefs have released their first injury report ahead of Week 9’s game against the New York Jets. Here's a quick breakdown of each team's Week 9 injury report. Keep in mind that clubs can add to the injury report through kickoff on Sunday. They will release game status designations on Friday, Nov. 6. Kansas City Chiefs' Wednesday injury report for Week 9 New York Jets' Wednesday injury report for Week 9 Aaron Glenn described Harrison Phillips and Garrett Wilson as day-to-day. Everyone else is “trending in the right direction.” VJ Payne’s practice window opened; he remains on injured reserve. However, a full practice means he should be activated for Week 9, unless he suffers a setback.

away.headline: Jets vs Chiefs: Garrett Wilson headlines Jets’ inactives
away.blurb: Garrett Wilson will not be suiting up for the New York Jets when they take on the Kansas City Chiefs today. Wilson is in the concussion protocol and will miss his first game this season. Wilson’s absence will be a problem for the Jets passing game in a game when they will need every weapon they can find. However, unlike past years, the Jets have some pretty good weapons even without Wilson, including rookies Omar Cooper and Kenyon Sadiq and young veteran Adonai Mitchell. Together with the return of Breece Hall to the lineup and the emergence of Braelon Allen as one of the best young backs in the game, the Jets should be able to compensate fairly well for the loss of Wilson. The full Jets inactive list for today’s game is as follows: Joseph Ossai has been a disatrous free agent signing for the Jets thus far. He has missed all but three games with various injuries, and when he has played, he hasn’t been very effective. Signed for three years and $36+ million in this past offseason, Ossai has been a costly mistake to date. Perhaps he will eventually prove otherwise if he can just get healthy. Another issue on the above list is Nahshon Wright. Wright signed with the Jets in the offseason after earning a Pro Bowl nod last year with the Chicago Bears. He has been active for just three games for the Jets. He has played just 22 snaps, all on special teams. Unlike Ossai, health hasn’t been the issue for Wright. He just hasn’t been good enough to crack the lineup. It probably would behoove the Jets to move Wright at the trade deadline, assuming there is any market for him.

away.headline: New York Jets rule out superstar WR for matchup vs. Kansas City Chiefs
away.blurb: With Wilson officially ruled out in Week 9, fans should expect to see New York utilize wideouts Tim Patrick, Omar Cooper Jr., Malik McClain, and Isaiah Williams more in its passing game when the Jets face the Chiefs on Sunday. This article originally appeared on Chiefs Wire: New York Jets rule out superstar WR for matchup vs. Kansas City Chiefs NFL insider Adam Schefter revealed that the New York Jets will be without star wide receiver Garrett Wilson when they face the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 9. Wilson — who started his professional career as the No. 10 pick in the first round of the 2022 NFL Draft — has been in the league's concussion protocol and missed all of New York's practice sessions ahead of the Jets' tilt against the Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium. The 2022 NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year started his tenure in New York with three 1,000-yard seasons as the Jets' top wideout, but saw his production dip when injuries derailed his 2025 campaign with the Jets.

home.headline: Chiefs in the market for WR after Xavier Worthy injury: report
home.blurb: Keep an eye out for any news regarding the Chiefs adding an offensive weapon this week. The Kansas City Chiefs are rumored to be in conversations about trading for a wide receiver ahead of the NFL ‘s deadline on Tuesday. On Sunday after the team’s 35-12 win over the New York Jets, those discussions only increased after the Chiefs lost receiver Xavier Worthy towards the end of the game with a hamstring injury. It’s unknown how severe his injury is and if he’ll miss any time, but the possibility of his absence makes the Chiefs more motivated to shop for a receiver. CBS’s Tracy Wolfson said on Sunday’s broadcast that general manager Brett Veach told her before the game that the team was in the market for a wide receiver ahead of Tuesday, and now with Worthy’s injury, it’s expected for them to make a trade happen. “As we’ve been talking about the lack of deep threats for the Chiefs, and I spoke with GM Brett Veach before the game, he told me that as the trade deadline approaches, the focus continues to be at that wide receiver position,” Wolfson said. “There has been increased dialogue this week, and he found that some of the major franchise players they looked at are off the market, but they will continue to have conversations over the next 24 hours to see if they can get something done by the trade deadline.” A few names have been linked to the Chiefs as rumors continue circulating. Indianapolis Colts’ Josh Downs requested a trade, and he pops up as an option for KC. The Jacksonville Jaguars have been more hesitant to listen to trade offers for their receiver Brian Thomas Jr., but the Chiefs are rumored to be interested in him. Jauan Jennings may have told the San Francisco 49ers that he liked his new home with the Minnesota Vikings, but he’s only playing on a one-year deal—he could easily be traded before the deadline. In the meantime, the Chiefs will rely on Rashee Rice as their top wide receiver. Tight end Travis Kelce still leads the Chiefs with 410 receiving yards. Through eight games, Worthy caught 33-of-47 passes thrown to him for 278 yards and one touchdown. On Sunday specifically, Worthy caught all six passes thrown to him for 48 yards.
