home.headline: Report: Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes avoids major elbow injury
home.blurb: "Patrick took a pretty good shot to the throwing arm today and came off the field in some pain. We checked him out right away and he told us his elbow was sore, but he was determined to get back out there," Reid said. "He returned, made some throws, and kept competing the way he always does. He's one of the toughest players I've ever coached, and he doesn't like missing snaps." Nov 09 (Field Level Media) - Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes avoided a major injury to his right elbow, according to a media report Sunday night. An MRI exam revealed an elbow strain or sprain but no significant damage, NFL Network reported. Mahomes will be monitored for pain and swelling over the next few days, leaving his status uncertain for next Sunday's game against the host Atlanta Falcons. Mahomes injured his throwing arm during Kansas City's 35-12 victory over the New York Jets. He completed 23 of 31 passes for 242 yards and two touchdowns but said afterward that his arm did not feel right early in the second half. "From the stories you hear, whenever you can grab the ball and try to throw it, you can't throw," Mahomes said. "Once I threw the football, I knew it wasn't -- hopefully, I haven't done the test yet -- it wasn't ligament-type stuff, it was more muscle-type stuff." Mahomes was drilled by Jets rookie edge rusher David Bailey while raring back to fire a pass downfield with 1:33 left in the first half. He came off the field supporting his right elbow with his left arm and appeared to be in significant pain. Head coach Andy Reid said the Chiefs would follow all of the proper steps to confirm Mahomes is not hurt. If upcoming tests give the Chiefs pause, Reid said the plan will be to "prepare Justin (Fields)" to face the Falcons on Sunday. Fields did not attempt a pass Sunday but ran twice for minus-1 yard. Mahomes returned to start Week 1 after sustaining a season-ending left knee injury in 2025.

home.headline: Jets vs Chiefs: Garrett Wilson headlines Jets’ inactives
home.blurb: Garrett Wilson will not be suiting up for the New York Jets when they take on the Kansas City Chiefs today. Wilson is in the concussion protocol and will miss his first game this season. Wilson’s absence will be a problem for the Jets passing game in a game when they will need every weapon they can find. However, unlike past years, the Jets have some pretty good weapons even without Wilson, including rookies Omar Cooper and Kenyon Sadiq and young veteran Adonai Mitchell. Together with the return of Breece Hall to the lineup and the emergence of Braelon Allen as one of the best young backs in the game, the Jets should be able to compensate fairly well for the loss of Wilson. The full Jets inactive list for today’s game is as follows: Joseph Ossai has been a disatrous free agent signing for the Jets thus far. He has missed all but three games with various injuries, and when he has played, he hasn’t been very effective. Signed for three years and $36+ million in this past offseason, Ossai has been a costly mistake to date. Perhaps he will eventually prove otherwise if he can just get healthy. Another issue on the above list is Nahshon Wright. Wright signed with the Jets in the offseason after earning a Pro Bowl nod last year with the Chicago Bears. He has been active for just three games for the Jets. He has played just 22 snaps, all on special teams. Unlike Ossai, health hasn’t been the issue for Wright. He just hasn’t been good enough to crack the lineup. It probably would behoove the Jets to move Wright at the trade deadline, assuming there is any market for him.

Led by first-year head coach Jeff Hafley, the Dolphins have struggled to do much right in 2026. Through seven games, they've scored the second-fewest points (16.7/contest), plus they've allowed the ninth-most points (25.9/game). Additionally, Miami did not notch its first win of the season until Week 7, defeating Aaron Glenn and the N.Y. Jets, 28-25. Undeniably, it's been a rough season for Hafley & Co., which find themselves in possession of the third-worst record in the NFL. The only teams which have been worse are the Tennessee Titans (1-7) and the L.A. Chargers (0-7). The Lions, under Dan Campbell, were once in the same unenviable shoes as the Dolphins. When Campbell first took over in the Motor City in 2021, Detroit was far from one of the most formidable teams in the NFL. Instead, just like the Dolphins currently, Campbell & Co. experienced their fair share of struggles and lost plenty of games on their way to establishing their tough, gritty identity. In fact, Detroit started the aforementioned campaign 0-10-1 before winning its first game in Week 13 against the Minnesota Vikings. In that sense, Campbell sees plenty of parallels between those Lions and this current iteration of Miami. “Coach Hafley’s done a good job in his first year,” the sixth-year Lions head man expressed to reporters this week. “A lot of similarities — it reminds me of what we were when we came in. They’re young, they’re hungry, they’re active, they run, they hit, they hustle, they finish, try to play disciplined ball. And they’re playing that way.” As much as Campbell's squad is undoubtedly the better team, you can't take anyone lightly in the NFL. And for as bad as the Dolphins have been, it's important to note they have not lost a game by more than seven points since Week 4. Their last double-digit loss came in Week 3 against the Kansas City Chiefs (24-10). And on top of all that, the Lions are severely banged up entering this Week 9 matchup , after suffering a plethora of injuries a week ago against Minnesota. They lost five total defensive players in the divisional tilt, including defensive captain Jack Campbell, the two best members of their secondary (Brian Branch and D.J. Reed) and EDGE DJ Wonnum. And they all are in danger of missing Detroit’s interconference contest in Miami. As a result, Miami – led under center by fifth-year passer Malik Willis – might have a chance to do some damage against Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard's unit . Yet, the Lions are seven-point favorites, per multiple sportsbooks, for a reason, and should emerge victorious in the road affair. At this present juncture, I'll give Detroit a 72 percent chance to secure the Week 9 victory . Campbell, 26, did not appear to be moving while he was taken off the field, as his teammates looked on with tears and concern. Campbell said Wednesday he is still working on regaining movement in his body, though he does have full movement in his lower body at this time. “I’m incredibly encouraged by the progress I’ve made in such a short period of time. I have full movement in my lower body, and I’m continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body,” he said in a statement. “I know there’s still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I’m taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better. My faith in God has never been stronger.” Jack Campbell #46 of the Detroit Lions lays on the ground after being injured on a play during the fourth quarter of a game against the Minnesota Vikings on Nov. 1. Mike Mulholland via Getty Images “I especially want to thank the athletic trainers and medical personnel who responded and cared for me on the field,” he added. “I know those were difficult moments, and I’m incredibly grateful for the professionalism, compassion, and care you showed me. The way you handled everything and looked after me when I needed it most is something I’ll never forget. From the bottom of my heart, thank you.” Dan Campbell, head coach for the Detroit Lions, previously spoke about visiting Campbell in the hospital, though he declined to share the specifics of his injury or his progress. “I got to go see him last night, it was good, it was positive,” Campbell said during a press conference on Monday. “Got to see his parents, talk to his wife, and everybody’s in good spirits. picks.blurb: Saints vs. Browns Predictions: Will New Orleans Take Advantage of Cleveland's QB Change? Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The New Orleans Saints will take on the Cleveland Browns at noon Sunday. The Saints are coming off a much-needed bye week after a 2-5 start to the year. Meanwhile, the Browns are off to an unexpected 5-3 start but will be without starter Deshaun Watson . Here are our staff predictions. Grant Chachere , Lead Writer: W 24-10 This is a game I would have picked the Saints to lose, but things change. Cleveland quarterback Deshaun Watson is questionable for Sunday’s game, so the organization will start Shedeur Sanders . Because of this revelation, it 100% benefits the Saints. Watson has been one of the league's better quarterbacks all season. However, with him out for this game, the Browns’ offense is less of a threat, even with solid receiving options in wide receiver Denzel Boston and tight end Harold Fannin . Then, add to the fact that left tackle Kelvin Banks is back after missing significant time due to an ankle injury and rookie wide receiver and first-round pick Jordyn Tyson will finally make his debut after suffering a hamstring injury during fall camp, the Saints’ odds of winning only increase. This is a great opportunity for the Saints to get a win, especially with a three-game slate coming up. However, if the Saints don’t get a win, there will be a lot more questions than answers in New Orleans, especially for head coach Kellen Moore and the man who hired him, general manager Mickey Loomis . Saints 24 Browns 10 Doug Joubert , Publisher: L 28-17 The Saints made some moves after the bye week, firing their run game coordinator and bringing in a familiar face at kicker. I asked earlier this week in my column if it was a step in the right direction or window dressing. This week also carries with it the return of Kelvin Banks Jr. from injured reserve after limited practice opportunities Wednesday, Thursday and Friday. Add to that first-round pick Jordyn Tyson makes his debut in a Saints regular-season uniform this weekend. The surprise move for me was the timing of cutting 4th year running back Kendre Miller . Though I have been on the "get rid of Miller ASAP" train for a while, I did not expect it to happen the day before a game. These moves force me to look back at the first half of the season and wonder if this Saints team has gotten better as the year has worn on. The answer is no. The kicking game move to Charlie Smyth is a lateral move, maybe a little better. The return of Banks will be an improvement, but the Saints weren't doing all that well running the ball with him in the lineup before the injury. Replacing a run coordinator cuts down the amount of feedback you're getting as a coach about your rushing attack. That could be good and bad. The defense cannot stop the run, while the offense can't get it going. This is not a good team. Some want to blame Mickey Loomis, some Kellen Moore, some want to put the onus on the athletes that have been brought into the fold (or kept). I say all that to say this: Even with Shedeur Sanders starting at quarterback Sunday for the Browns, a definite step back from the usual starter Watson, this Saints team has quite a lot to prove before I can say with confidence that they can scratch out a win. I would love for this to be the game where the Caesars Superdome regains its reputation as a hell-hole for visiting teams. I would love to see Audric Estimé be the back who makes the difference (the way Saints fans would love him to be) instead of a guy who has bounced around from practice squad to practice squad his entire career. I would like to have Chase Young continue to hunt down opposing quarterbacks, and while he's at it to stop the run, too. And I'd love to see the Saints win Sunday. I just don't see it. picks.blurb: Final Prediction for Saints-Browns Week 9 Matchup - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football MNF: Bills-Vikings live updates Week 10 Waiver Wire Jaguars' blockbuster deal Giannis left 'speechless' CFP doubling in size Final Prediction for Saints-Browns Week 9 Matchup Caleb Yaccarino · Roundtable Sports Sun, November 8, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads After two weeks without New Orleans Saints football, we are finally back. The Saints are also making their return to New Orleans, which may honestly be bad news for this team. The Saints have been unable to win a game at home this year, and some of their worst performances happened in New Orleans. For a team that has always valued the impact of playing at home, this is a really bad situation to be in, especially given how vocal fans can be. It also doesn't help that the pressure on the coaching staff to perform is palpable. The Saints also made some really important changes before this game. The Saints fired run game coordinator T.J. Paganetti, and they cut some players, including kicker Daniel Carlson and RB Kendre Miller. Each move made sense, and it is the first time we have seen real consequences from Kellen Moore's coaching staff. As I mentioned, the pressure is on this team, so we might as well try new things. For their opponent, it is a winnable game. The Cleveland Browns have been surprisingly one of the best teams in the NFL this season. They have had to make some crazy comebacks to make it happen, but QB Deshaun Watson is having a resurgence in his career. The defense is also playing really well, with the pass rush and pass defense standing out. But Watson is likely going to be out for this game. As of now, Watson has missed practice all week and is questionable for Sunday, so Shedeur Sanders will likely start for Cleveland. Although Sanders has not played yet this year, the Saints shouldn't overlook what the young QB can do. He had ups and downs throughout his rookie year, and if he is on point when facing the Saints' defense, it can be difficult to stop. The real worry for New Orleans is the Browns' defense. They have had run defense issues, so if the Saints defy all odds and fix the run game, that could be a way to win this game, but the rest of the defense will cause issues for the Saints. Now on to the prediction. Even with Watson likely being out, it's extremely difficult for me to choose the Saints. I do think it's going to be a close game, just not a victory for New Orleans. They need to prove the changes actually mattered first before I can believe something will change. For the score, I have the Browns winning 30-28.

away.blurb: The Browns will start Sanders, even though Watson has yet to be ruled out for Week 9. He hasn't practiced much this week, and even if he does somehow clear concussion protocol, the Browns will roll with Sanders as the starter for one week. Cleveland could give Sanders the Week 9 and Week 10 start before the team's Week 11 bye, where they could figure out who should be the starting QB for the remainder of the year. away.headline: Saints' Jordyn Tyson reportedly set to make NFL debut vs. Browns after hamstring injury
away.blurb: For more from Bleacher Report, check out our B/R app , homepage and social feeds—including Twitter , Instagram , Facebook , TikTok and YouTube . New Orleans Saints rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson will make his NFL debut against the Cleveland Browns on Sunday, according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz . Tyson was selected with the No. 8 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, but a hamstring injury landed him on injured reserve during training camp. The Saints need to activate the rookie from injured reserve by Saturday afternoon for him to be eligible to play on Sunday. New Orleans has a 2-5 record, but remains in contention in a relatively weak NFC South. This article will be updated soon to provide more information and analysis.

away.headline: Saints center Erik McCoy injured in overtime win over Browns
away.blurb: McCoy was listed as questionable to return, but obviously did not. Saints coach Kellen Moore said after the game that ''We'll gather more information and they'll do all the testing tomorrow (Monday). We'll see what it is.'' William Sherman took McCoy's spot at center during the final two scoring drives. Sherman was also used as an extra offensive lineman throughout the day against the Browns, playing a total of 25 offensive snaps. Injuries have plagued McCoy for the last few seasons. A biceps injury ended his 2025 season after just seven games. Groin injuries also limited McCoy to only seven games during the 2024 season. This season, McCoy had started the first eight contests and had played all but two offensive snaps before his fourth quarter injury against the Browns. More updates will be available on Erik McCoy as he is evaluated early this week. If McCoy is to miss time, William Sherman is the most likely replacement at center. Another option could be to slide right guard Cesar Ruiz to center and plug either Sherman or rookie fourth-round pick Jeremiah Wright in at right guard. The 3-5 Saints will host the 3-5 Carolina Panthers for first place in the NFC South this coming Sunday in the Superdome. Center Erik McCoy of the New Orleans Saints left Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over the Cleveland Browns with a reported biceps injury. McCoy was likely injured during the Saints next-to-last drive of regulation. He was not in the lineup for either of the team's final two drives, a 55-yard touchdown march to take the lead late in the fourth quarter and a 74-yard touchdown drive in overtime that proved to be the winning score. Saints quarterback Tyler Shough was comfortable about the transition from McCoy to Sherman at center, saying after the game: ''It was clean, man. We practiced that a lot, being able to get snaps with him throughout the week. It just shows his preparation, shows who he is. He was unfazed and came in right away. … I was really proud of him and the entire O-line.” This article originally appeared on Saints Wire: Saints center Erik McCoy injured in overtime win over Browns

away.headline: The Saints make a decision on rookie WR Jordyn Tyson’s status ahead of Browns game
away.blurb: The New Orleans Saints plan to activate the rookie wide receiver off injured reserve for Sunday’s game against the Cleveland Browns, according to a report. Tyson, the eighth overall pick in this year’s draft, has been out since getting hurt Aug. 13 with a hamstring injury and missed the Saints’ first seven games, but he returned to practice this week. Tyson’s return should help a Saints offense that has been uneven this season. The Saints rank 14th in points per game, but 23rd in total offense. Most of the team’s struggles have centered around the run game — the Saints fired run game coordinator T.J. Paganetti on Monday — but Tyson provides another dynamic weapon in the passing game, which could help open up New Orleans’ rushing attack. The Saints had previously listed Tyson as questionable. NFL insider Jordan Schultz first reported the news. The Saints, too, had been patient with Tyson since drafting him. Though draft analysts were concerned about the receiver’s durability due to Tyson’s injury history in college, the Saints were confident that Tyson would be able to hold up in the NFL. They slow-played his reps in the spring as he recovered from a separate hamstring injury, and when Tyson got hurt again this summer, the Saints avoided setting a firm timeline for his recovery. Tyson, speaking to reporters Wednesday, said his hamstring now feels 100% and that he even feels “more explosive” after the injury. Coming into the year, the Giants were the least likely to win the NFC East, while the Eagles were the favorites to repeat as division champions and be the first of the group to win three consecutive division titles since Philly won four in a row in the early 2000s. Flash forward heading into Week 9, and it couldn't be more opposite with the Giants as the front-runner to win the NFC East for the first time in 15 years, last doing so when the franchise won its fourth Super Bowl in 2011. McCarthy makes the start Now these two long-standing, I-95 corridor rivals go head-to-head for the first time in 2026, with the last meeting coming in the Week 18 season finale in January. The Giants are coming off a bye in Week 8 after a stunning 27-21 overtime victory as 10-point underdogs on the road over the Houston Texans . On the other sideline, the Eagles are off to their worst (2-6) in more than a quarter century, with their current six-game losing streak being the longest since President Barack Obama was reelected for a second term in 2012. Our NFL prognosticators are: Art Stapleton ( Giants /NFL writer, NorthJersey.com), Bert Bainbridge (sports trending reporter/columnist, NorthJersey.com), Brian Marron (digital producer, NorthJersey.com), Chris Iseman (Rutgers writer, NorthJersey.com), Mike Dougherty (sports writer, lohud.com), Bob Jordan (sports editor, Asbury Park Press/APP.com) and Dave Rivera (sports editor, USA TODAY Northeast/NorthJersey.com). Giants vs Eagles Week 9 predictions, staff standings Art Stapleton: 4-2-1 Dave Rivera: 3-3-1 Bert Bainbridge: 2-4-1 Chris Iseman : 2-4-1 Bob Jordan: 2-4-1 Brian Marron: 2-4-1 Mike Dougherty: 1-5-1 Can the Giants continue their stranglehold on the East or will the Birds losing ways finally come to an end with an upset at home over Big Blue? Art Stapleton The pick: Giants 27, Eagles 23 Here's why: John Harbaugh's team had a great bye week, with Dallas' stunning overtime defeat to Arizona increasing Big Blue's lead in the NFC East without even playing. QB J.J. McCarthy was outstanding in his first start against the Texans, clicking downfield with WR Malik Nabers, who had his fourth straight 100-yard receiving game. The Giants have not won in Philadelphia since Tom Coughlin was head coach in 2013, and they have not scored an offensive TD there in a win since their Super Bowl season of 2011. It's time for the streak to end. Bert Bainbridge The pick: Giants 30, Eagles 17 Here's why: No one thought this would be the reality at the midway point of the season with the Giants in the driver seat in the NFC East and the Eagles in free fall mode. Fresh off a bye, the G-Men go into Philadelphia and defeat the Birds at Lincoln Financial Field for the first time in 13 years. The pick: Giants 27, Eagles 16 Here's why: The Eagles are spiraling as the key injuries continue to mount, especially on offense. The Giants are the better team right now, and are fresh off of a bye week. Expect Big Blue to earn a relatively comfortable win. The pick: Giants 34, Eagles 20 Here's why: The Eagles are a mess right now and that's a big reason why the Giants are in prime position to win the NFC East. The pick: Giants 23, Eagles 16 Here's why: The Eagles are going nowhere this season, and with the Cowboys and Commanders not showing to be real threats in the NFC East at this point, John Harbaugh and the Giants are seizing the opportunity. Mike Dougherty The pick: Giants 27, Eagles 17 Here's why: After six consecutive losses, Eagles coach Nick Sirianni vowed his team would keep fighting. Those are not words usually heard in early November. A high-intensity start by the Giants should remove any drama from this one. The pick: Giants 22, Eagles 19 Here's why: J.J. McCarthy may not be Y.A. Tittle but doesn't have to be with Harbaugh's spiffy after-a-bye record (15–3, best among modern era head coaches with at least 10 games). My only question is how in the world the Giants are only favored by three points against a team that hasn't won since the Phillies were still a week away from finishing their regular season. The offense is ravaged by injury, and the defense is deteriorating before our eyes: 90 points and nearly 1,200 yards allowed in the last three games. Gimme Big Blue -3, and even make another bet at -6.5. Picks: Giants -3 Passing Props (O/U) JJ McCarthy: 214.5 passing yards, 1.5 TD (+174/-240), 0.5 INT (-130/-102), 17.5 completions, 29.5 attempts Joe Milton: 188.5 passing yards, 0.5 TD (-225/+164) 0.5 INT (-162/+122), 17.5 completions, 31.5 attempts Analysis: Milton is a total wild card. This will be his first NFL start, and he'll battle a strange Giants pass defense: 3 rd in yards allowed, yet 30 th in sacks per attempt. My theory is that the promotion of Milton to starter is less strategy than it is the fact he can run for his life when he needs to, something Tanner McKee doesn't do nearly as well or readily. McCarthy had a solid game in his first start for the Giants last week vs Houston. He threw for 252 yards, but six completions accounted for 182 of those yards. away.headline: Giants reveal severity of QB JJ McCarthy’s injury
away.blurb: Luckily, McCarthy was able to return to the game and lead the Giants to victory while completing 12 of his 19 passes for 127 yards. The No. 10 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft out of Michigan, McCarthy has thrown for 2,254 yards, 12 touchdowns and 13 interceptions in his professional career. New York Giants quarterback JJ McCarthy exited the team’s Week 9 win over the Philadelphia Eagles after taking a massive hit from linebacker Zack Baun. He eventually returned to the game after a trip to the locker room, but the team has since revealed if it could affect his playing status moving forward. According to NFL insider Adam Schefter of ESPN , McCarthy suffered a hip pointer and the team is confident that he will be ready for Thursday night’s game against the Washington Commanders. That is certainly good news, given how the injury initially looked. He was in visible pain on the sideline before heading to the locker room and being replaced by backup quarterback Jameis Winston. The Giants traded a 2027 fifth-round draft pick to the Minnesota Vikings in exchange for McCarthy following starter Jaxson Dart’s season-ending injury in September. New York then switched to McCarthy as its starter ahead of its Week 7 matchup against the Houston Texans, and he has played quite well since, throwing for 622 yards, one touchdown and one interception. away.blurb: The second-year back missed practice on Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday, receiving a "doubtful" designation on the team's final injury report . This week, Philadelphia will be thin at wide receiver once again. DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks were both ruled out for Sunday's game , leaving Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, and Hollywood Brown to take on the bulk of the receiving work. Giants could take huge steps to clinching the NFC East after return from bye week Injuries are a part of life in the NFL. No team is immune to the inevitable knocks that players take throughout the season. But it's hard not to feel like the New York Giants have had an unfortunate run of injury luck this year. Three of the most important players on the roster (Jaxson Dart, Brian Burns, and Tremaine Edmunds) have already sustained season-ending injuries. Both offensive tackles have been banged up at various points. Still, Big Blue sits atop the NFC East heading into a critical matchup with the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 9 . The injury woes haven't stopped, though. The G-Men could be without Cam Skattebo for this game, leaving their running back room alarmingly thin. With Friday's practice reports in the books, let's check in on the status of a couple of the Giants' most important injuries. Giants' final injury report before Week 9 Eagles matchup Skattebo suffered a hamstring injury during his long run in overtime against the Houston Texans. He put his body on the line for the win, literally. Even after the bye week, he still isn't trending toward playing on Sunday. If Skattebo doesn't play, the weight of the running back room will be placed on the shoulders of veteran Devin Singletary and rookie UDFA Greg Desrosiers Jr . In all likelihood, Phil Mafah would be promoted to the active roster to add a third option. Game Status: No Injury Designation After spending the entire offseason wondering about his recovery from the knee injury that ended his 2025 campaign, it was gut-wrenching to see Malik Nabers pop up on the injury report with a knee issue again. No need to worry, though; It looks like he'll be just fine. Nabers didn't practice on Thursday, but he was a full participant on Friday and doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game. It's a good thing he's ready to go, because the G-Men haven't found much production from the rest of their receiver room. As encouraging as Malachi Fields' progression has been, nobody wants to see him take on WR1 responsibilities against this Eagles secondary. All things considered, the Giants' injury report has been mostly positive this week. Skattebo may not suit up, but for the most part, this will be the same team that took down the Texans. DeVonta Smith injury leaves Giants' defense with no excuses The Giants can't complain too much about injury luck, at least not while the Eagles are around. They've lost their starting quarterback for the year, too, and the injury bug has worked its way through the rest of the roster. New York

Although the Commanders' 2-4-1 record is far from impressive, they remain a dangerous team that can win on any given Sunday. Commanders head coach Dan Quinn is currently fighting for his job , and injuries have plagued the team throughout a disappointing season. Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels has missed several games this season after aggravating a previous arm injury, while several other key players have been sidelined for significant periods of time. While they are 2-4-1, the Commanders still have an opportunity to win the weak NFC East. The Commanders just won their second game of the season after defeating the Philadelphia Eagles and currently sit third in the division. This season, the Commanders are 17th in points per game and 26th in points allowed. They have also struggled on third down, converting just 32% of their attempts, while their defense has surrendered too many points. Although the Commanders have been one of the worst teams this season, they have found success running the ball. Led by their dual-threat quarterback, they average 127 rushing yards per game and protect the ball with only three turnovers. The Commanders' biggest weakness lies in their passing defense, which ranks 27th in the league, allowing 243 yards per game and an opponent passer rating of 100.6. The Rams' success largely depends on quarterback Matthew Stafford's ability to effectively move the ball. Stafford is reportedly dealing with soreness in his right arm. He left the locker room after the Chargers game with a bag of ice on his right elbow. This could be a big game for Puka Nacua . Held to only 80 yards in Week 9, Nacua might have over 100 receiving yards this week. The Rams should still find success running the ball, but the overall game will depend on Stafford's effectiveness passing the ball. In a must-win game for the Rams, this news comes at the worst time. picks.blurb: Myles Garrett picks up 3.0 sacks in return, Rams beat Commanders 20-13 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football MNF: Bills-Vikings live updates Week 10 Waiver Wire Jaguars' blockbuster deal Giannis left 'speechless' CFP doubling in size Myles Garrett picks up 3.0 sacks in return, Rams beat Commanders 20-13 LANDOVER, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 08: Myles Garrett #95 celebrates with Aaron Donald #99 of the Los Angeles Rams after sack against the Washington Commanders during the fourth quarter at Northwest Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) (Getty Images) Myles Simmons · ProFootball Talk on NBC Sports Sun, November 8, 2026 at 9:17 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Welcome back, Myles Garrett. The star edge rusher returned from a knee procedure and showed the difference he can make, racking up 3.0 sacks in the Rams' 20-13 victory over the Commanders on Sunday afternoon. Garrett's first sack also forced a fumble, as he poked the ball out from quarterback Jayden Daniels in the second quarter. That led to a field goal late in the half, which cut Washington's lead to 10-6 at halftime. Garrett then had two more in the fourth quarter, one of which came after he'd just been flagged for an offside penalty. While Garrett starred on defense, receiver Puka Nacua paced the offense with 14 catches for 150 yards with a touchdown. His 14 receptions are the third-most he's had in a single game in his career. He also had a pair of carries for 20 yards. The Commanders had a 10-6 lead at halftime from a 37-yard field goal and a 7-yard touchdown pass from Jayden Daniels to Van Jefferson. The Rams got two field goals from Brandon McManus for their six points. But the Rams were able to double up with a touchdown on their first drive of the second half. Blake Corum ran it in for a 1-yard score to cap an eight-play, 69-yard drive. And while a Matthew Stafford interception allowed the Commanders to tie the game at 13-13, Stanford then threw a touchdown to Nacua to put the Rams ahead for good. Washington had a chance to at least tie the game late, but time ran out on their last drive. Daniels finished the game 24-of-35 for 273 yards with a touchdown. He had four carries for 16 yards. Stafford finished 26-of-43 for 228 yards with a TD and a pick. At 5-4, the Rams are now above .500 for the first time this season and on a three-game winning streak. The team will be on the road to face division-rival Arizona next weekend before a Week 11 bye. The Commanders have fallen to 2-5-1. They won't have much time to think about their missed opportunities, as they'll face the Giants on Thursday night in Week 10.

away.headline: NFL analyst is worried about Rams star Puka Nacua’s longevity after latest injuries
away.blurb: One NFL analyst expressed great concern about Los Angeles Rams star receiver Puka Nacua ’s long-term success in the league following his latest injury this season. Nacua shines as one of the best receivers in the NFL, giving Los Angeles a case for serious playoff contention. However, he suffered an MCL/PCL sprain as he will miss several weeks. NFL insider Marc Spears provided his thoughts on Nacua’s injury during his Monday appearance on NFL GameDay. He has concerns about the receiver’s longevity given his injury history. “If you think about how much he’s been hurt, and he’s been hurt because of his physicality in play. He’s not afraid to go across the middle, he seeks contact after he catches the football, he takes shots in games where you like, damn, is he even gonna get up from those shots? So I think more than anything right now with the Rams, because this is going to be your number one receiver. Davante was playing great, but Davante was brought in to complement Puka Nacua based on all of the things that he did in this offense,” Spears said. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “I don’t know how you circumvent it. I don’t know how you change any of that, but I am concerned about Puka Nacua and the Los Angeles Rams and the longevity, and I don’t want to be cheated of a great player like him. Because if you think about, there’s a laundry list of injuries now that’s starting to mount up with Puka’s career, and it’s a direct reflection in how he plays, unfortunately.” Los Angeles has a 5-4 record this season, sitting at third place in the NFC West Division standings. They are above the Arizona Cardinals while trailing the Seattle Seahawks and the San Francisco 49ers. In terms of the conference standings, they are ninth place. They lead over the Dallas Cowboys and the New Orleans Saints while being under the Seahawks and the Green Bay Packers. The Rams will begin preparations for their next road matchup. They take on the Cardinals in Week 10 as kickoff commences on Nov. 15 at 4:05 p.m. ET. Like ClutchPoints’ content? Be sure to follow us. away.headline: Puka Nacua injury: Rams WR to undergo MRI after suffering knee injury on final snap, per report
away.blurb: The Los Angeles Rams are holding their breath over the status of star wideout Puka Nacua. The All-Pro pass catcher is set to undergo an MRI on his knee after injuring it late in the team's Week 9 win over the Washington Commanders , according to a report from ESPN . The team reportedly does not believe Nacua suffered a torn ACL, but the imaging set to be done on Monday will determine the severity of the injury. Nacua suffered the injury on the final offensive snap of the game for Los Angeles with 1:44 remaining in the fourth quarter. He took a third-and-11 handoff from Matthew Stafford for a 5-yard gain. Nacua got up after a hard hit, but the injury will now be further evaluated. This injury dampens what was otherwise a stellar day for the wideout. He finished with 14 receptions on 19 targets for 150 yards and a touchdown, while adding 20 yards rushing. Nacua was the key to the Rams' success in the 20-13 victory that helped bring Los Angeles back over .500 on the season. Nacua is slated to miss time, which further dents what is already a banged-up receiver room. The Rams have already placed fellow wideout Davante Adams on injured reserve due to a ruptured hamstring he suffered in Week 6 against the Cardinals . That injury is expected to sideline him for anywhere from six to 10 weeks when he suffered it. This isn't the first injury Nacua has sustained this season, previously missing time this season with a hip injury. When he's been on the field, however, he's been among the best wideouts in the NFL and has caught a touchdown in four of his last five games played. If he's going to miss any time with this latest injury, it could embolden the Rams to make a move for a receiver prior to Tuesday's trade deadline.

away.headline: Commanders-Rams final injury report rules out two receivers, leaves McDuffie questionable
away.blurb: The Washington Commanders released their final injury report Friday ahead of their matchup with the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday. The report listed two of Washington's receivers, Treylon Burks (foot) and Dyami Brown (calf), as officially OUT against the Rams. Burks missed practice all week with an injured foot that he's been dealing with since the 49ers game, while Brown was added to Thursday's report as limited before missing Friday's practice. With Terry McLaurin already out for the season, Washington will need more from Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams, who led the team with seven targets and five catches for 54 yards against Philadelphia . Van Jefferson could see more work, and Luke McCaffrey is another option. Commanders head coach Dan Quinn spoke Friday about Jefferson's readiness: "I liked his approach. I liked his readiness, and so when called upon, I'd expect he'd play well." Rookie Jaden Bradley could also be elevated from the practice squad, although Washington hasn't announced that move. Elsewhere on the report, Jer'Zhan Newton is questionable with his pectoral injury despite practicing fully all three days. Newton is still in his 21-day practice window and must be activated from injured reserve before he can play. That decision carries some weight with Daron Payne and Javon Kinlaw now on IR . Shy Tuttle (shoulder) was limited all week but carries no game designation, while Sam Cosmi (knee) returned to full participation Friday. John Bates (shoulder) was limited throughout the week but has no game designation either. Los Angeles has some injury problems of its own, particularly in the secondary . Cornerback Jaylen Watson (shoulder) is out, while Trent McDuffie (back) is questionable after missing every practice this week. Former Commanders safety Kam Curl (foot) is also questionable after returning to limited practice Friday. The Rams could be short-handed in the secondary, although McDuffie's and Curl's availability won't be settled until closer to kickoff. The Rams also listed long snapper Joe Cardona (ankle) as doubtful, with tight end Colby Parkinson (ribs), linebacker Grant Stuard (hamstring), and receiver Jordan Whittington (back) questionable. Quarterback Matthew Stafford practiced fully throughout the week, while head coach Sean McVay expects Myles Garrett to play Sunday, pending his activation from injured reserve. Tight end Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring) was ruled out after injuring his hamstring in Friday’s practice . away.headline: Rams EDGE Myles Garrett’s huge injury return is a Los Angeles first since Aaron Donald
away.blurb: Los Angeles Rams defensive end Myles Garrett made an immediate impact in his return, notching three sacks and forcing a fumble during Sunday’s 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders. The performance put the 30-year-old in rare company, as he became the first player in franchise history to record three sacks and a forced fumble since star pass rusher Aaron Donald accomplished the feat back in 2020. His first sack came in the second quarter when he knocked the ball out of quarterback Jayden Daniels’ hands. Linebacker Omar Speights recovered the fumble, helping Los Angeles get into position for a field goal that reduced Washington’s advantage to 10-6 before halftime. Garrett added two more sacks in the fourth quarter, including one against Daniels after coming around left tackle Brandon Coleman. His final takedown turned out to be a game-changer, as he beat the replacement center with a quick move through the middle to prevent the Commanders from building momentum during their late comeback attempt. Garrett’s return helped Los Angeles improve to 5-4, extend its winning streak to three games and move above .500 for the first time this season. The Rams will next face the division-rival Arizona Cardinals before entering its Week 11 bye. Garrett, who underwent knee surgery in mid-September after initially attempting to play through the injury, missed seven weeks before returning to action in Week 9. The reigning Defensive Player of the Year wasted little time demonstrating his value, generating six quarterback pressures on 27 pass-rush attempts, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. He also managed a 22.2% pressure rate while playing 35 of the Rams’ 58 defensive snaps. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The three-sack performance was Garrett’s ninth career game with at least three sacks, the most by any player since Hall of Famer DeMarcus Ware in 2014, according to ESPN Research. He also brought his career sack total to 128.5, tying Hall of Famer Jared Allen for the second-most sacks by a player through his first 10 NFL seasons since the statistic became official in 1982. The contest also was the first time Garrett shared the field with Donald , who retired in March 2024. Across 23 plays with both defensive stars on the field, the Rams surrendered just 5.0 yards per play and recorded four sacks. During the other 19 plays, the defense allowed 8.0 yards per play and a touchdown without producing a sack. Like ClutchPoints’ content? Be sure to follow us. picks.blurb: Mile High Roundtable Drops its Predictions & Picks for Broncos-Panthers Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Denver Broncos are 6-2 at the midway point, riding a four-game winning streak. After defeating the Kansas City Chiefs last week, the Broncos now lead in the AFC West . If the Broncos want to retain their position atop the divisional mountain, they must take care of business and beat the teams they're supposed to. The 3-4 Carolina Panthers may seem like just another sub-.500 opponent, but they can be dangerous. The Broncos must guard against the "trap-game" nature of this matchup and handle the Panthers on the road. It's an East Coast road game with an early start, which has traditionally been an obstacle for the Broncos, but not since Sean Payton became the head coach in 2023. The Broncos have turned that particular ship around. The Panthers have some young playmakers on offense and a defense that's better than some people realize. But if the Broncos play up to their potential, it's hard to see the Panthers keeping up with them. That's a big if , though, as the Broncos have been frustratingly inconsistent on both sides of the ball, despite their winning streak. How will this shake out? Let's go around the table to see how the Denver Broncos On SI Mile High Huddle staff see this one unfolding on Sunday. Keith Cummings ( @KeithC_NFL ) 6-2 : East Coast road swings are never easy. Thankfully, the Broncos are a team that knows how to win late. Against the Panthers, the Broncos get an early lead and use Jonah Coleman to the maximum in a lopsided win. Pick : Broncos 31, Panthers 17 Chad Jensen ( @ChadNJensen ) 6-2 : Thanks to all his years in New Orleans, Payton has a special place in his heart for NFC South opponents; he's undefeated against them as Broncos head coach. Bo Nix is 4-0, including a 28-14 drubbing against the Panthers in 2024. Outdueling Bryce Young won't be quite so easy this time around, though, as the Panthers' young quarterback has improved dramatically since then, but Nix's confidence has come flooding back over the past two weeks, and that leads to a romping day for the Broncos' offense on the road. Nix has his best statistical game of the year, with 280 passing yards and three touchdown passes. Pick : Broncos 31, Panthers 16 Zack Kelberman ( @KelbermanNFL ) 6-2 : Unlike some, I’m not buying into the "trap game" element for the Broncos, facing a lesser opponent, an early East Coast game, right before their bye. away.headline: Broncos' Week 9 injury report: S Brandon Jones trending toward inactive
away.blurb: Denver Broncos starting safety Brandon Jones was among three players who missed practice for a second consecutive day and now appear highly questionable to play in Week 9 against the Carolina Panthers. Jones suffered a hamstring injury in last week's victory over the Chiefs and has yet to resume practicing. Ditto for defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike, whose shoulder issue has held him out. Ditto for cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine, who's dealing with an ankle affliction. Each player will need to get in at least a limited session Friday to have any chance of suiting up at Carolina. In more fortunate news, Denver's other starting safety, Talanoa Hufanga, was upgraded from DNP (Did Not Practice) to a limited participant on Thursday, giving him a shot at returning after being sidelined for the last three games with his own ankle malady. WRs Jaylen Waddle (chest) and Pat Bryant (ankle) were full participants, as well. Bryant will return from a four-game absence due to an ankle injury. On Carolina's side, five players did not practice: OLBs Jaelan Phillips and Trevis Gipson, CB Will Lee, OG Damien Lewis, and LB Bobby Okereke. Quarterback Bryce Young (ankle) was a full participant and will play against the Broncos. Assuming Jones is ruled out, Taylor Rapp would likely fill in as a starting safety at Carolina. If Hufanga can't go, Devon Key or JL Skinner would slot in next to Rapp. Skinner, in particular, had a standout game in last week's comeback victory over the Chiefs . Assuming Abrams-Draine is out of commission, second-year CB Jahdae Barron could see an uptick in snaps behind CBs Patrick Surtain II, Riley Moss, and Ja'Quan McMillian. Wide receiver Courtland Sutton and defensive end Zach Allen were also upgraded to full following a veteran rest day on Wednesday. Both will be active in Week 9. “You’ve definitely seen his ascension, and he’s very comfortable with what they’re doing," Broncos head coach Sean Payton said of Young on Wednesday. "It’s an explosive team. I think they’re seventh or eighth in explosives. They do a great job mixing the play action, the ‘RPO’ (Run-Pass Option) game. They’ve drafted well. So all those numbers are different today than they were two years ago.” Assuming Uwazurike is scratched, Sai'vion Jones would likely be penciled in as a starting DE opposite Allen, with third-round rookie DL Tyler Onyedim a possibility to make his NFL debut. away.headline: Broncos final injury report: Pat Bryant's return, depth on defense tested
away.blurb: The Broncos play the Carolina Panthers in Week 9, and it's the team's final game before the Week 10 bye, which comes at a perfect time. The team's final injury report does test the depth of this defense but also sees the return of a key rotational player on offense. All of Dondrea Tillman, Talanoa Hufanga, Kris Abrams-Draine, Brandon Jones, and Eyioma Uwazurike are either out or questionable in Week 9: Even with Bryant being listed as questionable, he'll play in Week 9: Hufanga's return will be the key to watch, and if you look at Denver's injury report from Week 8, there seems to be a good chance that the starting safety returns: In this practice week, Hufanga went DNP, Limited, and Limited and is listed as questionable. Just last week, the Broncos saw both Zach Allen and Jaylen Waddle have the exact same practice week, and both were also listed as questionable. Both played, so there is reason to believe that the Broncos took Hufanga's practice statuses this week with the same idea in mind. It does flat-out stink that the Broncos are going to still be down a starting safety with a likely Hufanga return. Jones hurt his hamstring during the win over Kansas City in Week 8 and did not practice all week. This article was originally published on predominantlyorange.com as Broncos final injury report: Pat Bryant's return, depth on defense tested . For the most part, the Denver Broncos have stayed healthy this year, but they have dealt with a good bit of injuries to primary depth, rotational players. We have already seen Jonah Coleman spent time on IR. Tyler Badie and RJ Harvey are both on IR, along with Jonah Elliss. The team has also seen Pat Bryant be placed on IR. Patrick Surtain II just recently missed time as well. All in all, Denver is certainly no strangers to injuries this year, but, for the most part, the primary starters are healthy and in a good spot. Denver Broncos final injury report for Week 9 against the Panthers In an ideal world, both Tillman and Hufanga suit up. If not, the depth of this defense is going to be tested big-time. The offense is clearly much healthier, as every one of the primary starters are healthy enough to play. I guess if we had to 'pick' one side to be hurt more, it would be the defense given how good this unit has been for years now, but that doesn't make this week's report any less shaky. The Broncos getting a win in Week 9. moving to 7-2, and having two weeks off would be the absolute best-case scenario. Denver's bye would allow every banged-up player to get healthier, and it would also present a perfect opportunity for the team to add a player or two at the NFL Trade Deadline and get them up to speed with the bye. Even in a loss, the Broncos sitting at 6-3 would still position themselves well down the stretch, especially with the ease of the remaining schedule. The Panthers will be experimenting a bunch this week. They’ll presumably shake the personnel up along the offensive line, and they’ll have a new defensive coach calling plays. Such risks might work out for them, kind of like how their RPOs stunned the Lions’ defense on Sunday Night Football (gosh, that feels like a lifetime ago!). Even still, I think the Broncos are too talented on defense and too disciplined on offense to let a winnable game like this slip away. Sunday, they’ll want to steady the ship. And they will have to pull off an upset to do so. The Panthers (3-4) still sit atop the NFC South, but in order to hold onto their station, they’ll likely need to emerge from Bank of America Stadium with a victory against one of the powers of the AFC — the Denver Broncos (6-2). The Sean Payton-led team has won its last four contests, including a 28-24 thriller against the Chiefs. Another flattering Broncos stat: They’re 15-0 in their last 15 regular-season one-score games . Payton’s record against the Panthers, according to Pro Football Reference, is 19-13, including the only win as Broncos head coach against the Panthers in 2024. Houston is averaging 23.6 ppg (12th) compared to a league-worst 14.1 points per contest for the Los Angeles Chargers , one of the games in our Week 9 against-the-spread picks . I also expect a long day for Justin Herbert , who has already been sacked 23 times. He's up against a Texans pass rush that has the fifth-most sacks in the AFC . Houston has also won both road games this season, and I expect the Texans to cover on Sunday. Texans vs Chargers combo I expect a low-scoring Week 9 affair. Even though the Chargers have been particularly solid at defending in the red zone, Collins is my strongest look among Week 9 anytime touchdown picks on Sunday. Los Angeles remains the only winless team in the NFL. They are certainly one of the league's more disappointing teams, and the Texans are in the same boat. The Chargers (0-7) will host the Texans (2-5) this Sunday. The two teams are nowhere near where they expected to be, but they'll hope this week helps one of them turn the tide. Here are four bold predictions for Week 9. J ustin Herbert throws for 300+ yards and one touchdown Herbert is coming off a season-high 257 passing yards. The 28-year-old completed 24 of 32 passes, another season-high. Although he recorded two interceptions, Herbert showed clear signs of improvement. Houston's defense allows 244 passing yards per game, the fifth-most in the NFL, which helps Herbert build on his Week 8 performance. Chargers force C.J. Stroud into two t urnovers The Chargers' defense is far and away their best unit of the three. I expect them to wreak some havoc on Stroud, although he has taken exceptional care of the football. Stroud has 11 touchdowns to just one interception and no fumbles. However, I'm predicting the Texans quarterback has at least one interception and a forced fumble. Chargers running backs combine for 100+ rushing yards The Chargers offense hasn't rushed for 75+ in their last two games. Los Angeles rushed for 64 yards against the Rams, averaging 2.6 yards per carry. Omarion Hampton could see an increased role in the backfield, with a fierce pass rush led by Will Anderson and Danielle Hunter. The Texans' rush defense is allowing 3.8 yards per carry (9th) and 98.0 yards per game (11th). While the Chargers' rush offense hasn't been what we expected, I think they'll find a better groove in Week 9, despite their opponent. Chargers score two touchdowns After going 27 consecutive offensive drives without scoring a touchdown, the Chargers will get in the end zone, not once, but twice. One of those touchdowns will come through the air, while the other will be on the ground. away.headline: Justin Herbert injured, DJ Uiagalelei makes NFL debut as Chargers fall to 0-8 in loss to Texans
away.blurb: "Could be a fracture, we'll find out," Harbaugh told reporters after the game on Sunday. The Chargers quarterback, who went undrafted out of Florida State, came in for Herbert late in the fourth quarter as his team trailed big. The prospect of Uiagalelei taking the starting job from Herbert would have sounded like a joke coming into the season, but nothing is out of the realm of possibility amid an 0-8 start. Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert avoided a fractured finger after suffering an injury during Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Houston Texans, coach Jim Harbaugh revealed on Monday. Harbaugh said on Sunday that Herbert wanted to finish the game, but the coaching staff thought better of it. Herbert said he will do "whatever I can to make sure I'm 100 percent." While Harbaugh noted Herbert wanted to play through the injury, the coach opted to have DJ Uiagalelei—who made his NFL debut on Sunday—finish the game. Uiagalelei's first drive ended with a touchdown pass. Uiagalelei finished his first NFL game with 24 yards and a touchdown on 2-of-7 passing. It had been another rough day for Herbert before he exited, as he had just 193 yards, a touchdown and an interception. Herbert came into the game with 1,398 passing yards, five touchdowns and 10 interceptions. Before Sunday, he hadn't thrown a touchdown pass since Week 5. The Chargers' hopes of reaching the playoffs are essentially over at this point, but bringing in a new starting quarterback could give the team a spark heading into the second half of the season. Uiagalelei had a five-year college career with Clemson, Oregon State and Florida State, though he never quite lived up to the hype he had coming into college. After going undrafted in 2025, he signed with the Chargers but didn't make the 53-man roster. He spent last season on the team's practice squad. Over the offseason, he competed for the backup position behind Herbert but ultimately lost to Trey Lance and started the year on the practice squad. After Lance was placed on the injured reserve with a groin injury in September, Uiagalelei was promoted to the active roster, paving the way for him to serve as Herbert's backup.

away.headline: C.J. Stroud tosses 5 TD passes as Texans rout winless Chargers 44-22. LA finally scores a TD
away.blurb: “I could have done a better job of getting the ball out quicker,” Herbert said. “I mean, they’re very good. They have a premier pass rush, and I got to do a better job getting the ball out.” “We’ll have to figure it out and keep looking and doing our best to keep getting better because it hasn’t been good enough yet,” Herbert said. Chargers: CB Isas Waxter (ankle) got hurt in the first quarter and didn't return. ... DL Justin Eboigbe (ankle) got hurt in the first quarter, but returned. ... WR Ladd McConkey was active, but had back spasms before kickoff and didn't play. INGLEWOOD, Calif. (AP) — C.J. Stroud had been feeling lousy all week, barely practiced and woke up with chills on game day. Then he had his version of Michael Jordan's flu game. Stroud threw five touchdown passes, including a pair of season-best 63-yarders to Tank Dell and Kayshon Boutte, and the Houston Texans routed the winless Los Angeles Chargers 44-22 on Sunday. “I don't know what I had but was not feeling good,” Stroud said. “My teammates really helped me. Just to have that type of performance under the weather a little bit was to me a testament to our team and our resilience.” Throwing to four different receivers, Stroud came up one TD short of the franchise record of six TDs. He smiled at the comparison to Jordan, who overcame flu-like symptoms to famously score 38 points for the Chicago Bulls in Game 5 of the 1997 NBA Finals. “Not there yet,” he said, “but maybe one day.” Stroud completed 21 of 35 passes for 384 yards with one interception and one sack. “I beat myself up a lot when I don’t do great, so I’m going to enjoy this,” he said, eager to reunite with friends and family after the game not far from his hometown of Rancho Cucamonga. Houston (3-5) has won three of four after starting the season 0-4. “I’m proud of our guys for getting back to repping our style of play,” Texans coach DeMeco Ryans said. “C.J. has brought elite execution and playmaking ability. He really gives that confidence to the entire team.” The Chargers (0-8) ended a 37-drive touchdown drought when Quentin Johnston caught Justin Herbert's 58-yard scoring pass in the fourth quarter. It was their first TD since Oct. 11 against Denver. Their 22 points were the second most they've scored in a game this season. “That was a positive,” coach Jim Harbaugh said. Soon after, Herbert was wearing a large white glove on his left hand to protect a finger taped by trainers. “Shouldn't be an issue,” he said afterward. He was replaced by DJ Uiagalelei, who threw his first career TD pass, a 15-yarder to Derius Davis, his first scoring catch since December 2024. The Chargers had scored 24 points on field goals during their TD drought. Cameron Dicker had three, including a season-best 52-yarder, on Sunday. Herbert finished 13 of 23 for 193 yards and an interception and was sacked a career-high eight times. He has been sacked 31 times this season, the second most in the league. away.headline: After Further Review: Texans HC DeMeco Ryans comments on win vs. Chargers
away.blurb: Q: On whether he anticipates S Reed Blankenship and RB David Montgomery to return to practice Ryans: “The biggest factor is confidence. That's the one thing that stands out to me. Another cool thing about C.J. is what he did over the summer, spending time with all the receivers, having them come out to work out with him. He organized workouts and had those guys make sure they showed up so they can work on their timing, work on their chemistry. That's what I see. I see us benefiting a lot from him and his leadership from the summer. That's showing up now because of how he took the time to think about his teammates and make sure everybody came out and got some work in together with him. I think it says a lot about his leadership, says a lot about him and just how dialed in he is. Now you see that confidence, you see that chemistry, you see it really at the highest level that it's been since we've been here.” Ryans: "For a lot of people, for a lot of guys, seeing is believing. I think going out, putting the work in, but actually seeing it actually come true, it means a lot. I think that's part of earning the confidence. You have to see it. You put the work in, you go out, you play well, you go get a win and now, ‘Can you repeat the behavior?’ It's really about the process. It's really about the time, the effort that you put in throughout the week and then that shows up on Sunday in different forms. But if you have a good week, it truly will show up on Sunday and that's what I'm most proud of. The way they prepared throughout the week, they were able to see the benefits of that on Sunday because everybody, each area, did what they had to do to win the game. Each area played really well and we still have things to clean up in all three areas. But I'm proud of the effort, proud of just how we went out and how we finished that game.” Ryans: “Special teams guys have a lot of time to themselves away from the team when we're not working specific special teams, team-oriented drills; those guys are off to the side. When you talk about detailing out your craft, it's something that goes unnoticed, but that snap, hold, kick process- there's a lot of timing that goes to how we want the laces to be handled. ‘When are the laces showing up back to the holder? That's what I love about the preparation and the work that they do. They're always striving for more. That's what makes it exciting when they operate on game day. It looks seamless, but it's not. home.headline: Justin Herbert injured, DJ Uiagalelei makes NFL debut as Chargers fall to 0-8 in loss to Texans
home.blurb: "Could be a fracture, we'll find out," Harbaugh told reporters after the game on Sunday. The Chargers quarterback, who went undrafted out of Florida State, came in for Herbert late in the fourth quarter as his team trailed big. The prospect of Uiagalelei taking the starting job from Herbert would have sounded like a joke coming into the season, but nothing is out of the realm of possibility amid an 0-8 start. Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert avoided a fractured finger after suffering an injury during Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Houston Texans, coach Jim Harbaugh revealed on Monday. Harbaugh said on Sunday that Herbert wanted to finish the game, but the coaching staff thought better of it. Herbert said he will do "whatever I can to make sure I'm 100 percent." While Harbaugh noted Herbert wanted to play through the injury, the coach opted to have DJ Uiagalelei—who made his NFL debut on Sunday—finish the game. Uiagalelei's first drive ended with a touchdown pass. Uiagalelei finished his first NFL game with 24 yards and a touchdown on 2-of-7 passing. It had been another rough day for Herbert before he exited, as he had just 193 yards, a touchdown and an interception. Herbert came into the game with 1,398 passing yards, five touchdowns and 10 interceptions. Before Sunday, he hadn't thrown a touchdown pass since Week 5. The Chargers' hopes of reaching the playoffs are essentially over at this point, but bringing in a new starting quarterback could give the team a spark heading into the second half of the season. Uiagalelei had a five-year college career with Clemson, Oregon State and Florida State, though he never quite lived up to the hype he had coming into college. After going undrafted in 2025, he signed with the Chargers but didn't make the 53-man roster. He spent last season on the team's practice squad. Over the offseason, he competed for the backup position behind Herbert but ultimately lost to Trey Lance and started the year on the practice squad. After Lance was placed on the injured reserve with a groin injury in September, Uiagalelei was promoted to the active roster, paving the way for him to serve as Herbert's backup.

home.headline: C.J. Stroud tosses 5 TD passes as Texans rout winless Chargers 44-22. LA finally scores a TD
home.blurb: “I could have done a better job of getting the ball out quicker,” Herbert said. “I mean, they’re very good. They have a premier pass rush, and I got to do a better job getting the ball out.” “We’ll have to figure it out and keep looking and doing our best to keep getting better because it hasn’t been good enough yet,” Herbert said. WR Ladd McConkey was active, but had back spasms before kickoff and didn't play. INGLEWOOD, Calif. (AP) — C.J. Stroud had been feeling lousy all week, barely practiced and woke up with chills on game day. Then he had his version of Michael Jordan's flu game. Stroud threw five touchdown passes, including a pair of season-best 63-yarders to Tank Dell and Kayshon Boutte, and the Houston Texans routed the winless Los Angeles Chargers 44-22 on Sunday. “I don't know what I had but was not feeling good,” Stroud said. “My teammates really helped me. Just to have that type of performance under the weather a little bit was to me a testament to our team and our resilience.” Throwing to four different receivers, Stroud came up one TD short of the franchise record of six TDs. He smiled at the comparison to Jordan, who overcame flu-like symptoms to famously score 38 points for the Chicago Bulls in Game 5 of the 1997 NBA Finals. “Not there yet,” he said, “but maybe one day.” Stroud completed 21 of 35 passes for 384 yards with one interception and one sack. “I beat myself up a lot when I don’t do great, so I’m going to enjoy this,” he said, eager to reunite with friends and family after the game not far from his hometown of Rancho Cucamonga. Houston (3-5) has won three of four after starting the season 0-4. “I’m proud of our guys for getting back to repping our style of play,” Texans coach DeMeco Ryans said. “C.J. has brought elite execution and playmaking ability. He really gives that confidence to the entire team.” The Chargers (0-8) ended a 37-drive touchdown drought when Quentin Johnston caught Justin Herbert's 58-yard scoring pass in the fourth quarter. It was their first TD since Oct. 11 against Denver. Their 22 points were the second most they've scored in a game this season. “That was a positive,” coach Jim Harbaugh said. Soon after, Herbert was wearing a large white glove on his left hand to protect a finger taped by trainers. “Shouldn't be an issue,” he said afterward. He was replaced by DJ Uiagalelei, who threw his first career TD pass, a 15-yarder to Derius Davis, his first scoring catch since December 2024. The Chargers had scored 24 points on field goals during their TD drought. Cameron Dicker had three, including a season-best 52-yarder, on Sunday. Herbert finished 13 of 23 for 193 yards and an interception and was sacked a career-high eight times. He has been sacked 31 times this season, the second most in the league. home.headline: After Further Review: Texans HC DeMeco Ryans comments on win vs. Chargers
home.blurb: Q: On whether he anticipates S Reed Blankenship and RB David Montgomery to return to practice Ryans: “The biggest factor is confidence. That's the one thing that stands out to me. Another cool thing about C.J. is what he did over the summer, spending time with all the receivers, having them come out to work out with him. He organized workouts and had those guys make sure they showed up so they can work on their timing, work on their chemistry. That's what I see. I see us benefiting a lot from him and his leadership from the summer. That's showing up now because of how he took the time to think about his teammates and make sure everybody came out and got some work in together with him. I think it says a lot about his leadership, says a lot about him and just how dialed in he is. Now you see that confidence, you see that chemistry, you see it really at the highest level that it's been since we've been here.” Ryans: "For a lot of people, for a lot of guys, seeing is believing. I think going out, putting the work in, but actually seeing it actually come true, it means a lot. I think that's part of earning the confidence. You have to see it. You put the work in, you go out, you play well, you go get a win and now, ‘Can you repeat the behavior?’ It's really about the process. It's really about the time, the effort that you put in throughout the week and then that shows up on Sunday in different forms. But if you have a good week, it truly will show up on Sunday and that's what I'm most proud of. The way they prepared throughout the week, they were able to see the benefits of that on Sunday because everybody, each area, did what they had to do to win the game. Each area played really well and we still have things to clean up in all three areas. But I'm proud of the effort, proud of just how we went out and how we finished that game.” Ryans: “Special teams guys have a lot of time to themselves away from the team when we're not working specific special teams, team-oriented drills; those guys are off to the side. When you talk about detailing out your craft, it's something that goes unnoticed, but that snap, hold, kick process- there's a lot of timing that goes to how we want the laces to be handled. ‘When are the laces showing up back to the holder? It’s not who you play but when you play them. The Green Bay Packers will face the New England Patriots on Sunday. It’s a measuring-stick game for the Packers, who believe they are Super Bowl contenders. The Patriots played in the Super Bowl last year and believe they have the goods to take the next step. With a top-tier quarterback and coach and a strong defense, they will be a formidable challenge. The Patriots, however, will play without their top two receivers, A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs. Their premier tight end, Hunter Henry, is questionable with a foot injury that held him out of practice to start the week. Their starting guards, Alijah Vera-Tucker and Mike Onwenu, are on injured reserve. So is their top pass rusher, Harold Landry. Can the Packers take advantage of the “when you play them” part of that adage? Here are our weekly game predictions. Bill Huber’s Packers-Patriots Prediction The Packers have had some good fortune this season. They faced the Buccaneers without Baker Mayfield and the Bears without Caleb Williams. They will have more good fortune against the Patriots. While Drake Maye, last year’s MVP runner-up, will be the starting quarterback, he’s going to be playing with an incredibly shorthanded group of receivers. Mack Hollins, DeMario Douglas and Kyle Williams are not the same as A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs. Good quarterbacks can make it work with whoever, so this won’t be a layup victory for Jonathan Gannon’s defense. However, New England’s pass protection has been leaky, with Maye facing the fourth-highest pressure rate in the league. Can the Patriots’ receivers get open before the Packers’ pass rush arrives on the scene? Added together, the game has been put on a silver platter for Green Bay’s defense to be the most powerful unit on the field. On the other side of the ball, it’s going to be a challenging day for Jordan Love, as well. The Packers, of course, can’t run the football, and it’s having an impact on the passing game with the play-action attack having become irrelevant . If the Packers can’t run the ball – and what reason is there to believe they will? – they’re going to have to deal with the teeth of the Patriots’ strong pass rush, which ranks fifth in sack percentage. Elijah Ponder – the best pass rusher that nobody has ever heard of – is seventh in the league with six sacks. With 3.5 sacks, Christian Barmore powers the interior rush. “He’s a really good player,” Packers coach Matt LaFleur said of Ponder, an undrafted free agent last year. “To be truthful, I hadn’t heard a whole lot about him until I started watching the tape and I’m like who is this guy? What’s his story? How do we not know about him? Everybody knows about him now. When you look at their edges, all three of those guys that are really doing the bulk of the work are really good players, and you couple that with the interior guys, it’s a really formidable front.” That could mean limited time for Christian Watson and Matthew Golden to beat the premier cornerback duo of Christian Gonzalez and Carlton Davis. “Really good DBs,” Love said. “I think they do a lot of things very well. I think as anything, it’s a challenge for me, for the receivers on the outside to be able to go see how good we can be and how good we can attack them and make plays against them. I think they do a really good job. I think Gonzalez is definitely one of the best in the league and he makes plays. I feel like for us, it’s a fun test.” Ultimately, I’m taking the Packers, who are 3-point underdogs at FanDuel Sportsbook . Both quarterbacks are really good, but I’ll take Watson and Golden vs. Gonzalez and Davis over Hollins and Douglas vs. Keisean Nixon and Brandon Cisse. In a close game, the Packers will fail to run out the clock but the defense will save the day. And they’ll need it, with the Bears and Lions favored to win their games against the Buccaneers and Dolphins, respectively, while the first-place Vikings are underdogs against Buffalo. Bill’s Prediction: Packers 24, Patriots 20. Bill’s Record: 6-2. Jacob Westendorf’s Packers-Patriots Prediction Everything outside of the field favors New England in this game with the return of Rob Gronkowski and Tom Brady, which has been discussed all week. The reality on the field, however, is that the Packers have more healthy players than the Patriots do. The Patriots are missing their top two receivers and their starting tight end is going to be hobbled, at minimum, if he can play. Drake Maye and Jordon Love are both being asked to carry a heavy load, but Love has a better supporting cast around him. In addition, Jonathan Gannon should be able to create enough confusion for Maye to make a couple of mistakes that swing the game in the Packers’ favor. Jacob’s Prediction: Packers 24, Patriots 17.
