So do the New England Patriots, who lost in last year’s Super Bowl. On Sunday, these storied teams will collide in Foxborough in what is truly a measuring-stick game for the Packers. The Patriots are three-point favorites. With Tom Brady on the call and Rob Gronkowski being inducted into the team’s Hall of Fame, here are three reasons why the Packers will spoil the party and earn a statement win. 1. Depleted Patriots Offense The Patriots reached the Super Bowl last year despite the lack of a legit threat at receiver. So, they attempted to rectify that problem by signing Romeo Doubs, who had a solid four seasons with the Packers, and trading for A.J. Brown, a three-time Pro Bowler who had surpassed 1,000 yards in six of his first seven seasons. Neither player will be on the field for this game, though. Doubs is on injured reserve with a shoulder injury and Brown is out again with a knee injury. Combined with the questionable status of top tight end Hunter Henry, who leads the team in receptions, the Packers’ strong defense will face a diluted New England attack. Without Brown and Doubs and with Henry limited to eight snaps with an injured foot, the Patriots needed to rally past the lowly Dolphins last week. The Patriots were held to merely 313 yards. The key for the Packers will be limiting the Rhamondre Stevenson-led running game and putting the pressure on New England’s passing game to make plays against a Packers defense that ranks fourth in opponent passer rating. “I think first of all, he’s an elite quarterback in the pocket, out of the pocket,” cornerback Brandon Cisse said of Drake Maye. “He’s extremely dangerous. He can make any throw. Obviously, he’s super-smart. “They got a great offensive coordinator, great receivers, great playmakers around him and, obviously, when the run game’s going they can do everything and they can throw it just as good as they can run it. So, we’re going to have our hands full for sure and got to make sure that we’re ready to play.” Prediction: The Patriots are going to have a hard time stringing together sustained success on offense. 2. Drake Maye May Screw Up Patriots quarterback Drake Maye is one of the best in the business. He was one vote away from winning NFL MVP last year. However, unless you’re one of the undisputed elite quarterbacks, a quarterback oftentimes is only as good as his supporting cast. So, while Maye is seventh in completion percentage, third in yards per attempt and fifth in touchdowns, only three quarterbacks have thrown more than Maye’s eight interceptions and his six fumbles are one off the unwelcome NFL lead. “I think speaking from playing zone coverage, they’ve got great eyes,” Maye told reporters this week. “They got eyes on the quarterback, they make plays on the football. They can, obviously, catch well. The safeties are great players. They do a lot of things well and they read the quarterback very well, mix up in zone looks. Tip balls have turned into picks that they’ve shown. “So, they’ve just had a habit of creating turnovers in the pocket with the quarterback. They have got some free rushers’ help, too, of the quarterback panicking and trying to fit some stuff to tight windows. They’re good at keeping you in some negative plays. They make you go longer distances. It’s hard.” In the Patriots’ three losses, Maye has thrown three touchdowns vs. six interceptions. In the five wins, it’s 12 touchdowns and two interceptions. His eight interceptions equal last year’s total (in less than half the attempts) are only two off his total from his rookie season in 2024. Prediction: It only takes one big mistake to swing a game between equal teams. Based on this season, Maye is more apt to make that mistake. 3. Turnovers (And Taking Advantage of Them) “The ball” is the most important thing in the sport, coach Matt LaFleur likes to say. Teams that take away and protect the ball tend to win; teams that don’t tend to lose. The Packers are tied for fourth in the league at plus-4 in turnovers. After creating only 14 takeaways last season – when Micah Parsons was on the field for 14 games – they rank second in the league with 15 takeaways this season. The Patriots this year are minus-7 overall; only the white-flag-of-surrender-waving Colts are worse at minus-11. Their 15 giveaways are the third-most in the league. Added together, you get this chart. Points Off Turnovers through Week 8 pic.twitter.com/UmVq9xw7uU The Packers are third in the league by scoring 52 points off takeaways; the Patriots are tied for 23rd with 20 points off takeaways. Green Bay’s aggressive, playmaking defense works hand-in-hand with quarterback Jordan Love’s aggressive, playmaking approach to the position. “Nobody’s had more 20-yard pass plays,” Patriots coach Mike Vrabel told reporters on Wednesday. “(Love is) a quarterback that’s wildly efficient. He has a few off-days, but they’re few and far between. They throw shots. They’ve, obviously, great speed on the edges. They have an excellent tight end, Tucker Kraft, and now getting [Josh] Jacobs back, it seems like they’re trying to work him back in there a little bit more and see what he can do for them in the red zone and things like that. I think they’ve protected better the last few games. “I think that when one of your best players for them is their quarterback, or their best player, that’s an emphasis that they try to make because when you give him time, he’s able to find [Matthew] Golden, [Christian] Watson or Tucker Kraft. Defensively, very physical. They have the second-most negative plays and created the second-most negative plays in the league. Seventeen percent of their drives end in a turnover, so that leads the league, as well.” Love is cooking. He and Kirk Cousins are the only quarterbacks with at least two touchdown passes in seven games this season. “Our goal every week is to go 1-0, and this is a very good team,” Love said. “Like you mentioned, they were in the Super Bowl last year for a reason. They’re very good in, really, all three phases. They got an elite defense. I think they do a lot of things really well. They got two really good corners on the outside. “Yeah, I got a lot of respect for them. It’s always a good test, but I think the goal for us to see how we can go out there and execute the plan, and the goal is to come away victorious. We know to put ourselves in the best position late in the season. We got to really just win every game, and that’s the mindset of going 1-0 every week. It’ll be a good test for us.” Prediction: The Packers have at least two takeaways in five consecutive games. If they can do it again, they’ll win. Drake Maye and Jordan Love have been some of the best passers in the NFL this season and their Sunday matchup should be a good one. Even though the Packers are sitting in the basement of the NFC North, this game will be a good measuring stick for the Patriots as they look to remain in contention for the top spot in the AFC East. Ahead of Week 9, Patriots On SI beat reporters Ethan Hurwitz and Zac Ventola break down how the game will unfold, which players will be x-factors and predict a final score. Who do you think is right? Hurwitz: Make Things Difficult For Jordan Love New England Patriots linebacker Josh Uche (55) and Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love (10) dive for a fumbled snap during their preseason football game Saturday, August 19, 2023, at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wis. Tork Mason/USA TODAY NETWORK-Wisconsin | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Love has been playing really well this season , especially when it comes to uncorking it and launching it deep. Whether it's Matthew Golden, Christian Watson or Tucker Kraft, the Packers have several guys that can stress the back-end of the Patriots' secondary. They'll need to find a way to limit Green Bay's explosive threats past the sticks. But that's easier said than done. Love has been playing really well this season , especially when it comes to uncorking it and launching it deep. Whether it's Matthew Golden, Christian Watson or Tucker Kraft, the Packers have several guys that can stress the back-end of the Patriots' secondary. They'll need to find a way to limit Green Bay's explosive threats past the sticks. But that's easier said than done. "A really, really intelligent quarterback, talented, athletic," Mike Vrabel said of Love about what he saw from him coming out of college. "I think all those things have proven to be true. His poise and composure at the line of scrimmage, I think he's worked on cadences, and the operation has really improved from a young quarterback coming out." X-Factor: WR Mack Hollins (if activated) Without A.J. Brown for the second-straight week and Romeo Doubs still on IR, the Patriots continue to deal with a depleted wide receiver room (DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams, Efton Chism III). If the Patriots choose to activate Hollins off of IR for this game, they'd be able to get some much-needed size back at the position. Hollins hasn't played since Week 4 after dealing with a calf injury suffered in Buffalo, and returned to practice this week. Final Score Prediction: Patriots 28, Packers 23 The Patriots, despite the slow start in Miami a week ago, feel like they're on a roll. In front of a national audience with Tom Brady calling his first Patriots game, I don't see how this week ends in a loss. What it will take is Maye slinging it just like he's done the last few games and use his legs to extend some plays — as well as not letting Green Bay's rushing attack with Josh Jacobs find its footing. Ventola: Nothing Short Of Perfection Sep 27, 2026; Jacksonville, Florida, USA; New England Patriots cornerback Marcus Jones (25) warms up before a game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at EverBank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Melina Myers-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect A week ago, the injury-riddled Patriots played an awful Dolphins squad and narrowly edged out a win. On Sunday, the still-injury-riddled Patriots will have to perform to their highest level for a chance to beat a Packers squad with playoff aspirations. A week ago, the injury-riddled Patriots played an awful Dolphins squad and narrowly edged out a win. On Sunday, the still-injury-riddled Patriots will have to perform to their highest level for a chance to beat a Packers squad with playoff aspirations. New England’s best chance at victory? Forcing Green Bay quarterback Jordan Love to make poor decisions. The Packers’ pass-heavy offense averages the second-most yards through the air in the NFL, and the fewest rush yards per game. Green Bay’s 28-year-old signal caller has thrown an interception in each of his past three games, an opportunity New England may need to capitalize on. X-Factor: CB Marcus Jones This season, Green Bay has relied heavily on second-year wide receiver Matthew Golden. The speedy pass catcher sits top-10 in the NFL in both receptions and receiving yards. I expect Jones to play a major part in attempting to slow down the wideout’s production on Sunday. Not to mention, Jones’ other role for the Patriots — punt returner — is one the Packers have stuffed all season long. Green Bay allows the second-fewest yards per punt return in the NFL. From locking down a star wideout to boosting the New England offense’s field position, Jones will play a pivotal role in his team’s success on Sunday. Final Score Prediction: Packers 30, Patriots 24 I would be shocked to see the short-staffed Patriots can pull off a win over this highly touted Packers squad. New England hardly had the talent to take down Miami a week ago. With the Patriots’ receiver room still highlighted by DeMario Douglas , Efton Chism and Kyle Williams, it feels hard to believe they can produce enough offensively to squeak out a win. But maybe — just maybe — a Super Bowl LI reunion, Tom Brady being back in Gillette Stadium and Rob Gronkowski being inducted into the team’s Hall of Fame might just bring the magic New England needs come Sunday. Tom Brady will be in the booth for his former team's Week 9 matchup, and the action at Gillette Stadium promises plenty of drama on the field too as the New England Patriots host the Green Bay Packers. With New England laying 3. 5 points as home favorites and the total set at 44. 5 points, my top Packers vs. Patriots predictions and NFL picks back Green Bay's relentless pass defense to steal the spotlight, keeping this affair close enough for the road underdogs to cover. It all gets started at 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX. TOP PICK Packers vs Patriots prediction today: Packers +3.5 I'm locking in the Green Bay Packers +3.5, down to +2.5 , because they have better net early-down EPA per play and a higher quarterback-pressure rate differential than the New England Patriots , and I like this matchup for Green Bay's defense. According to RBSDM.com, the Packers rank third in weighted defensive EPA per dropback . Drake Maye struggled against the Seahawks (fifth), Steelers (sixth), and Jaguars (fourth), completing just 63.8% of his passes with one touchdown and six interceptions. Packers defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon also gets extra prep time for a New England offense without wide receiver A.J. Brown and possibly without Mack Hollins and tight end Hunter Henry . Green Bay limits explosives, forcing Maye to work the ball methodically downfield, where we've already seen him make costly mistakes. Packers vs Patriots combo I expect Green Bay to dictate the terms defensively, but that doesn't mean the Packers need to win outright for me to cash. New England can move the chains without producing explosive plays, which helps running back Rhamondre Stevenson pile up receiving yards while keeping the game within one possession. Meanwhile, Green Bay doesn't need a monster offensive performance, either. One well-executed red-zone possession could be enough for tight end Tucker Kraft to find pay dirt. The beauty of this angle is that I don't need either quarterback to light up the scoreboard . In fact, a relatively ugly, low-scoring game could work perfectly fine for all three legs. Tucker Kraft anytime touchdown Rhamondre Stevenson Over 24.5 receiving yards Packers vs Patriots touchdown scorer: Tucker Kraft Tucker Kraft's anytime touchdown prop is good up to 30% . New England has excellent outside cornerbacks, but the middle of its defense is vulnerable in coverage. Per Pro Football Focus, three of the Patriots' four starting linebackers and safeties have failing coverage grades . Kraft was enjoying a career year before tearing his ACL around this time last season. He hasn't quite regained that form, but he's still a Pro Bowl-caliber tight end . With New England stronger on the outside than over the middle, I like Kraft's chances of finding the end zone. Packers vs Patriots player prop: Rhamondre Stevenson 25+ receiving yards Rhamondre Stevenson's 25+ receiving yards prop is tradable up to 55% . This correlates with my Green Bay +3.5 pick. I'm expecting the Packers to take away Drake Maye's deep ball and force him to check down, with Stevenson benefiting from RB TreVeyon Henderson being ruled out. Stevenson is New England's third-most targeted pass-catcher , partly because of injuries to the Patriots' WR corps. That's still an issue this week, with Brown out Sunday and Romeo Doubs on IR. The Patriots are 3-point favorites on the spread (Patriots -3), with the over/under set at 44.5 (-112o / -108u). The Patriots are -170 favorites on the moneyline and the Packers are +142 underdogs. Packers vs Patriots Odds Packers vs Patriots Spread : Packers +3 (-105), Patriots -3 (-115) Packers vs Patriots Over/Under : 44.5 (-112o / -108u) Packers vs Patriots Moneyline : Packers +142, Patriots -170 Packers vs Patriots Week 9 Preview The Packers under head coach Matt LaFleur have been an excellent team to back when they are priced as underdogs. LaFleur has covered 65.1% of all games when his team is catching points, and I believe this is another very good spot for Green Bay to potentially steal a victory. The narrative surrounding the Packers offense has to do with their lack of pass protection, as every mention of their future outlook as a Super Bowl contender is usually followed by a comment regarding their offensive line issues. Jordan Love is navigating those issues quite well, as it may be surprising to some that he has just a 32% pressure rate on all of his dropbacks. Only seven quarterbacks with 200 or more dropbacks have faced pressure less often than Love this season. We already know Green Bay struggles to run the football effectively, and that data point is completely baked into the line here. Sure, most of the offensive success for this team is squarely on the shoulders of Love, but that is something I am completely comfortable with against a Patriots team that ranks 26th in quick pressure percentage. Quick pressures occur within 2.5 seconds of the snap, and it is not something I am concerned about happening regularly in this matchup. If there is a signal caller who will be under constant duress in this game, it is likely to be Drake Maye . Maye has regained his MVP-level play from a season ago, but protection issues that plagued this team in the playoffs remain. The 44% pressure rate allowed by the New England offensive line is the highest rate league-wide. The Packers are generating pressure at the 12th-highest rate, but more importantly, they are converting those pressures into sacks. Green Bay has 22 sacks on the season, the sixth-most in the NFL. While the Packers' pass rush is undoubtedly above average, it has been the coverage in the secondary that has been this defense's biggest strength. Green Bay allows just 6.2 yards per pass attempt (fifth-best) while also ranking among the top five pass defenses in expected points added (EPA) per pass against. During Maye's hot streak, he has been doing his best work when throwing down the field. Maye leads the league in touchdown passes of 20 or more yards downfield this season, in addition to being efficient in the intermediate areas of the field. Over the past five weeks, Maye has completed 67% of his throws that have traveled more than 10 yards past the line of scrimmage. However, it is worth noting he has not played the most difficult slate of defenses during that stretch. The Packers are a completely different animal defensively than the teams Maye has shredded in recent weeks. During that same span of five games, Green Bay is second in the league in defensive EPA. The Packers specialize in limiting explosive plays — allowing the third-fewest of any defense in football. On throws 10 or more yards downfield, the Packers have allowed opposing quarterbacks to complete just 44% of their passes, generating seven interceptions while allowing just two touchdowns. The Patriots are not equipped to pressure Love as often as they need to, but the Packers do possess the tools to halt numerous New England possessions with their sticky coverage and timely pass rush led by Devonte Wyatt and Lukas Van Ness . Packers vs Patriots Spread Prediction, Betting Analysis Jordan Love and Drake Maye are in good form — both rank inside the top 12 of qualifying quarterbacks in adjusted net yards per attempt, have passer ratings that exceed 105.0 when kept clean and boast identical big-time throw rates. Let's call it a wash at quarterback. The team protecting their passer more cleanly also happens to be the team with the decided advantage defensively. Getting three points with the Packers in this spot is a tremendous value. New England didn't play the prettiest game on the field, but at this point for them, a win is a win. With all the injuries that the Patriots have seen take place, especially to the offense, the team has been able to stay alive. This week, the Patriots will be hosting the Green Bay Packers, giving the team a real challenge on its hands. Green Bay, like New England, has started to play much better of late, finally put things together on the field. The Packers will be entering the game with a record of 5-3, with both sides of the ball clicking for the team. New England is going to have to be careful in this game; otherwise, they could be on the losing end of the contest. Analysts Gary Davenport, Brad Gagnon, Kris Knox, Moe Moton, Brent Sobleski, Wes O'Donnell, and Ian Hanford of Bleacher Report all made picks for the game between the two teams. But six of the seven experts went with Green Bay to take down the Patriots in this matchup. Only Gagnon went with New England to win the game, despite this contest being played at home for the Patriots. But the Packers recent play likely has to do with how confident those around the league are heading into the week. One key for New England this week will be how quarterback Drake Maye performs, especially when it comes to turnovers. The Green Bay defense can be feisty at times, using its opportunistic nature to get the best of opposing quarterbacks. Maye will have to find a way to overcome the injuries that the Patriots have seen this year, going against this tough defense. But the veteran quarterback has done well this year , even with his issues earlier in the season. Against Green Bay, the Patriots may need to rely on the running game a little more, taking some pressure off Maye's shoulders. Head coach Mike Vrabel will have to put his signal-caller into a strong position to win, avoiding any issues. The offensive line will also need to hold up in the game, giving Maye time to throw the ball against this defensive front. Kickoff for the Patriots game against the Packers is scheduled to take place at 1:25 p.m. PT/4:25 p.m. ET at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough.

It feels like they're coming off a bye heading into Week 9's matchup with the New England Patriots. And to be fair, it was a mini-bye. The Packers last played on October 29 on Thursday Night Football. By the time you're reading this, that was 10 days ago. Double-digit days is a long time to go without playing football in the NFL. For the Packers, it was a chance to re-set after a 5-3 start, though. Frankly, it was a much-needed re-set, and hopefully it will have done this team well. There's still extremely injured and maddeningly inconsistent on this side of the mini-bye, but Jordan Love is playing like a potential MVP candidate , Jonathan Gannon's defense looks really good and oh...Micah Parsons is getting back to practice. That's right, the multi-time All-Pro is getting back to it, though he's not making any promises regarding his level of play. He's also likely not to be activated until the night before Thanksgiving, so he wont' play a role in this one. That is a shame, because the Packers are on the road against one of the better teams in the AFC in the 5-3 Patriots. Here's everything (else) you need to know about this game. Brown was supposed to be a huge addition this offseason for the Patriots, but he's appeared in just three games this season due to injury. Tight end Hunter Henry is hopeful that he'll play, but he was limited in practice on Friday and did not practice earlier in the week. Running back TreVeyon Henderson is scarily dealing with neurological symptoms . With all that firepower hampered, the Patriots are relaying on former 2023 sixth-round pick DeMario Douglas to fuel their offense. Douglas is having the best season of his career so far, with 26 catches for 332 yards and four touchdowns, but he's not the type of player the Pack will lose sleep game planning against. In the meantime, Packers' rookie second-round pick Brandon Cisse was the NFL's defensive rookie of the month after recording 21 tackles, seven passes defended, one interception and one sack in October. Cisse appears to be a rising star, and he should be able to neutralize Douglas when asked to go one-on-one with the former Liberty wideout. away.headline: Patriots inactives for NFL Week 9 vs. Packers
away.blurb: Already down A.J. Brown and TreVeyon Henderson, there was uncertainty surrounding another key member of the New England Patriots’ offense heading into Sunday’s game against the Green Bay Packers: tight end Hunter Henry entered the weekend listed as questionable on the injury report due to a foot injury he sustained last week in Miami. However, New England’s inactives list released 90 minutes before kickoff did not have the team captain listed among the five players ruled out. While it remains to be seen how involved Henry will be after participating in only one practice this week, his availability in itself is a positive. As noted above, TreVeyon Henderson (illness) and A.J. Brown (knee) were already ruled out on Friday. Joining them on the sidelines on Sunday is a late addition to the injury report: No. 4 cornerback Charles Woods was added as questionable with a hamstring injury less than an hour before inactives were due. The Packers had already ruled out four of their inactives before their trip to Foxborough, including starters Sean Rhyan (ankle), Travis Glover (knee) and Zaire Franklin (shin). No. 2 running back Marshawn Lloyd (knee) has now been added to the list. As for the other four players on the inactives list, they look like this: The two other inactives are both healthy scratches: Behren Morton is the team’s third quarterback, rookie Dametrious Crownover an emergency option at offensive tackle. This also means that only one of the Patriots’ seven original questionables is not good to go: interior offensive lineman Greg Van Roten, who remains on injured reserve after returning to practice on Wednesday. The others, a group including not just Henry but also wide receiver Mack Hollins (calf), right tackle Morgan Moses (foot), cornerback Carlton Davis III (neck), and safeties Kevin Byard III (chest) and Brenden Schooler (hamstring), have been given the green light. Kickoff between the Patriots and Packers at Gillette Stadium is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET .

home.blurb: He has at least seen some limited action this season with 50 carries for 244 yards and one touchdown. He impressed against the Green Bay Packers on Sunday with 55 yards and a score on the ground and will surely see plenty of opportunities against the Detroit Lions. Bleacher Report • 5h Report: Michael Wilson Out for Season The New England Patriots and fantasy football managers alike may need to turn elsewhere for the immediate future with running back Rhamondre Stevenson reportedly dealing with a knee injury. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Monday the veteran "is dealing with a knee tendon issue that is not expected to require surgery but could sideline him for a short period of time." NFL Network's Ian Rapoport added more context: It is another setback for the New England running back room, as TreVeyon Henderson missed the last two games with an illness. ESPN's Mike Reiss noted the depth chart is now Corey Kiner and Lan Larison ahead of Terrell Jennings, who is on the practice squad. From a fantasy perspective, managers who are completely desperate for running back options because of injuries or bye weeks could look at Kiner and Larison as waiver-wire pickups. After all, the Patriots have to play someone at the position with Stevenson and Henderson sidelined, and they are the next ones up. And if that is the case, Kiner is the obvious choice. ▶️ Full Packers-Patriots Recap 05:36 As for Larison, he has just three carries on the season. The bigger question is how long the Patriots will be without Stevenson in the middle of a playoff race. The loss to the Packers dropped them to 5-4 on the season, which is good enough for the seventh and final seed in the AFC playoff picture. They are tied with the Cleveland Browns and one game ahead of the Las Vegas Raiders and Baltimore Ravens, so just treading water without Stevenson may not be good enough to make the postseason. Stevenson hasn't even been that effective as a runner this season at just 3.9 yards per carry, which is tied for the lowest mark of his career. But he is a physical runner who can pick up the difficult yardage while remaining involved in the aerial attack with 26 catches for 258 yards and two scores. home.headline: Patriots inactives for NFL Week 9 vs. Packers
home.blurb: Already down A.J. Brown and TreVeyon Henderson, there was uncertainty surrounding another key member of the New England Patriots’ offense heading into Sunday’s game against the Green Bay Packers: tight end Hunter Henry entered the weekend listed as questionable on the injury report due to a foot injury he sustained last week in Miami. However, New England’s inactives list released 90 minutes before kickoff did not have the team captain listed among the five players ruled out. While it remains to be seen how involved Henry will be after participating in only one practice this week, his availability in itself is a positive. As noted above, TreVeyon Henderson (illness) and A.J. Brown (knee) were already ruled out on Friday. Joining them on the sidelines on Sunday is a late addition to the injury report: No. 4 cornerback Charles Woods was added as questionable with a hamstring injury less than an hour before inactives were due. The Packers had already ruled out four of their inactives before their trip to Foxborough, including starters Sean Rhyan (ankle), Travis Glover (knee) and Zaire Franklin (shin). No. 2 running back Marshawn Lloyd (knee) has now been added to the list. As for the other four players on the inactives list, they look like this: The two other inactives are both healthy scratches: Behren Morton is the team’s third quarterback, rookie Dametrious Crownover an emergency option at offensive tackle. This also means that only one of the Patriots’ seven original questionables is not good to go: interior offensive lineman Greg Van Roten, who remains on injured reserve after returning to practice on Wednesday. The others, a group including not just Henry but also wide receiver Mack Hollins (calf), right tackle Morgan Moses (foot), cornerback Carlton Davis III (neck), and safeties Kevin Byard III (chest) and Brenden Schooler (hamstring), have been given the green light. Kickoff between the Patriots and Packers at Gillette Stadium is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET .

Predicting the Raiders' Week 9 Moves In their Week 8 matchup against the Jets, Las Vegas made several notable changes to their starting lineup that proved fruitful. After struggling to find competent play at the right guard position between Jackson Powers-Johnson and Caleb Rogers, the Raiders turned to rookie Trey Zuhn. The Jets are not known for being a stout defense, but they are serviceable and gave Las Vegas fits for the entire first half, holding the Raiders to 97 total yards. Still, Zuhn looked like he may be the Raiders' best option at right guard for the rest of the season. Sunday's matchup against the 49ers will be much more telling, as San Francisco's defense is much more of a challenge than New York's. It will be interesting to see how Zuhn does at guard against one of the toughest teams the Raiders will face this season. If Zuhn plays well against the 49ers, the starting right guard position is his to lose. Starting Zuhn at right guard wasn't the only change Las Vegas made against the Jets. They also started rookie running back Mike Washington over Ashton Jeanty. The Raiders cannot afford to sit Jeanty for an entire game, as he is far too valuable catching the ball out of the backfield. Still, the way they successfully used Washington on the ground and Jeanty through the air against the Jets is worth building upon in Week 9 against the 49ers. Ahead of the team's road matchup against the 49ers, offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko praised Washington's Week 8 outing. “He’s somebody that continues to improve, really works his craft. He wants to get better at each and every single thing he does, whether it’s fitting his hands up, his eyes, everything coming out. It’s all the little fundamental things that we talk about. It’s stuff that he wants to get better at, improve on, and that’ll allow him to become a more successful player,” Janocko said earlier this week. “Running the ball is a full team thing. The greatest thing about football in general is that it’s 11 as one on every single play. So, it takes all 11 for everybody to be successful." Cornerback Darien Porter returned to practice this week after playing only one play against the New York Jets last Sunday. He is officially listed as questionable heading into Week 9. However, speed is arguably Porter's greatest asset on the field, and he is dealing with a groin injury. A groin injury can linger. Despite being listed as questionable, Kubiak and defensive coordinator Rob Leonard may decide not to risk damage to Porter's long-term health in a game where they already face an uphill battle. Las Vegas faced a similar decision earlier this season, when they could have rested running back Ashton Jeanty against a New England Patriots team that was missing more than five players before their matchup ended. The Raiders need Porter beyond just this week. Resting Porter on Sunday is far from ideal for Sunday's game, but may be best for his career, depending on the severity of his injury and how much progress he made on it during the week. Porter sitting out would offer a valuable opportunity to other corners on the roster. Porter may very well start against the 49ers. Regardless, rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses is sure to see significant playing time. Heading into Sunday, Masses could be in for another action-packed day, who has had extreme highs and lows during this season. “I think it’s always a moving target. See where your team’s at, and who’s playing the best ball at the time. And it’s a 17-game regular season where things change every week. And [there have] been changes at guard," Kubiak said earlier this week. "[We have] changed up front defensively. Changed at corner, and that’s the NFL. We have a young roster, and we’re going to give guys opportunities and see what fits us best." Charlie Disturco · Action Network Sun, November 8, 2026 at 8:23 PM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Las Vegas Raiders (4-4) battle the San Francisco 49ers (6-1) today in NFL Week 9. Kickoff is set for 4:25 p.m. ET from Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, Calif. The game will broadcast live on FOX. The 49ers are 8.5-point favorites on the spread, with the over/under set at 51.5 total points. San Francisco is a -440 moneyline favorite to win outright, while Las Vegas is a +340 underdog. Let's get into my Raiders vs 49ers predictions and player props . Raiders vs. 49ers Picks: Ashton Jeanty Over 27.5 Rushing Yards | Christian McCaffrey Over 60.5 Rushing Yards My Raiders vs. 49ers best bets are two props for Ashton Jeanty and Christian McCaffrey — both overs on their rushing yards. Make sure to find the best odds by checking our live NFL odds page. Raiders vs 49ers Odds Raiders vs 49ers Spread : Raiders +8.5 (-108), 49ers -8.5 (-112) Raiders vs 49ers Total : 51.5 (-118o / -102u) Raiders vs 49ers Moneyline : Raiders +340, 49ers -440 Raiders vs 49ers Preview It seemed like Fernando Mendoza was primed to take over the starting quarterback job as the Raiders spiraled into a four-game losing streak. But a collapse by the Jets kept Kirk Cousins in the driver's seat, and the veteran is expected to start again on Sunday. Despite the Raiders putting up 38 points, one storyline stole the headlines: Mike Washington Jr. handled 25 carries. Ashton Jeanty? Just two. Could that be tied to Jeanty's comments about the Jets' lack of interest in tackling in the week leading up to the game? Possibly. But Jeanty has also been largely inefficient, averaging just 2.2 yards per carry over the previous three weeks. The soft benching could serve as a wake-up call for Jeanty, although Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak still expects the workload split between Jeanty and Washington to vary week to week. I expect Jeanty to get a much larger share of the carries today. Washington didn't exactly make the most of his opportunity, averaging just 3.3 yards per carry on 25 attempts against New York. Despite a struggling run game, Cousins has kept the offense competitive. The Raiders rank sixth in the NFL in scoring at 27.6 points per game, with much of that production going through tight end Brock Bowers , who is averaging 91.2 receiving yards per game. Tre Tucker has emerged as a reliable receiving option thanks to his speed, but the rest of the wide receiver room remains thin. Jalen Nailor has gradually settled into the WR2 role, while Jack Bech continues to work his way back from injury. Defensively, the Raiders can't stop a nosebleed. Opponents have scored at least 30 points against Las Vegas in each of the last five weeks. The Raiders rank in the bottom three in both yards allowed per game (381.9) and points allowed per game (28.8). The 49ers' Week 8 bye came at the perfect time as they continue to deal with one of the most injury-riddled offenses in football. After opening the season with six straight wins, San Francisco fell to Atlanta. Christian McCaffrey battled through an injury and missed a large portion of the game, while the 49ers were also without Deebo Samuel and Mike Evans . Samuel and Evans are not expected to return Sunday, but the 49ers should get Demarcus Robinson back. McCaffrey also benefits from the extra rest and is good to go — a massive boost for an offense that runs through him. Despite all the injuries, the 49ers' offense continues to hum. Brock Purdy is playing like an MVP candidate, and San Francisco ranks among the league's top five in scoring at 28.1 points per game. However, it's the defense that has taken the biggest step forward this season. Fred Warner and Dre Greenlaw have elevated the linebacker group, while the midseason acquisition of DeForest Buckner gives the defensive line another dimension. Nick Bosa , who hasn't played since Week 2, also returns from injury today. Allowing fewer than 20 points per game, San Francisco may finally have the pieces to chase that elusive Super Bowl trophy. When healthy, this team can be a force to be reckoned with. Raiders vs 49ers Player Props, Picks There are two props I like in this one. The first is ugly and comes with plenty of uncertainty, but I'm willing to take the risk. I refuse to believe Klint Kubiak is going to make the same mistake twice and leave Ashton Jeanty behind Mike Washington Jr. on the depth chart. There's plenty of speculation surrounding this team, but Washington is not the answer. In fact, he's tied with Jacoby Brissett in broken tackles this season (one). Jeanty is far more explosive than Washington, particularly as a pass catcher. Has the Raiders' run game been a problem all season? Absolutely. But Jeanty's rushing yards prop set at 27.5 is simply too low for me to pass up. I'll hold my nose and back Jeanty, even with the Raiders entering as double-digit underdogs. The second prop centers around Christian McCaffrey. As always, the biggest concern with the superstar is injury risk. However, McCaffrey is coming off a bye week and got Wednesday off, which is standard treatment for many veteran players. He returned to practice Thursday and practiced in full on Friday. The Raiders' run defense has been putrid. We just saw Braelon Allen average 7.0 yards per carry against them last week, marking the seventh consecutive week an opponent has rushed for at least 100 yards. Las Vegas is currently allowing 5.31 yards per carry. Not only should the 49ers have plenty of success against this defense, but the game script could also lead to a more run-heavy approach. McCaffrey is averaging 4.6 yards per carry and has cleared this rushing yards line (60.5) in all five games in which he's played at least 55% of the snaps. Expect a fresher McCaffrey and plenty of success on the ground. picks.blurb: Raiders vs. 49ers expert picks and predictions ahead of Week 9 kickoff - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football MNF: Bills-Vikings live updates Week 10 Waiver Wire Jaguars' blockbuster deal Giannis left 'speechless' CFP doubling in size Raiders vs. 49ers expert picks and predictions ahead of Week 9 kickoff Marvin Uzor, Raiders Wire · Raiders Wire Sat, November 7, 2026 at 11:30 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Last week, the experts split almost evenly on Raiders vs. Jets , and the believers walked away looking smart. Seven days later, the panel has made up its mind. Across the 21 straight-up picks rounded up here, every single one goes to the San Francisco 49ers. There is a twist hiding in the scores, though. Seven of the 11 national score predictions have the Raiders losing by single digits, which would be enough to cover the spread. The Raiders Wire staff went 4-0 for the 49ers, with an average score of 31-23. LaMarr Fields had the widest margin at 34-23, pointing to a 49ers ground game the Raiders haven't been able to stop. NFL.com sees no drama All five NFL.com analysts took the 49ers, and nobody on that panel is harsher than Jeremy Bergman at 40-24. Bobby Kownack went 28-17, while Gennaro Filice (35-27), Dan Parr (34-26) and Brooke Cersosimo (28-20) kept it within eight. Only Bergman and Kownack have the 49ers winning by double digits. Cersosimo pointed to a familiar face on San Francisco's defensive line. Defensive tackle DeForest Buckner, reacquired from the Indianapolis Colts during the bye, is set for his second debut with the 49ers. "Buckner's addition should pay dividends for San Francisco moving forward, beginning Sunday against the visiting Raiders," Cersosimo wrote. She also acknowledged San Francisco's turnover problems before the bye, but she still gave the 49ers the edge in most major categories. CBS Sports and ESPN agree on the winner At CBS Sports, Pete Prisco has the 49ers winning 31-17 , while John Breech sees a tighter game at 30-23. ESPN's writers all picked San Francisco as well, with Pamela Maldonado at 24-20, Seth Walder at 29-23 and Eric Moody at 34-20. ESPN's Football Power Index gives the 49ers an 83.6% chance to win, a number that backs up the panel. Pro Football Talk expects a fight Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk also landed on 24-20, tied with Maldonado for the closest call among the national picks. He sounds ready for a scrap. "In a renewal of a rivalry so intense that they had to stop playing each other in the preseason, the Raiders will make it interesting," Florio wrote. The spread is where Raiders fans find friends USA TODAY's six experts, including Jarrett Bell and Nate Davis, went 6-0 for the 49ers straight up. Against the spread, Bleacher Report's panel leans Las Vegas 4-3 , with Gary Davenport, Ian Hanford, Wes O'Donnell and Brent Sobleski taking the points. Brad Gagnon, Kris Knox and Moe Moton laid them. Hanford admitted that "everything logical here is telling me to take the 49ers to win this one going away." He still expects quarterback Kirk Cousins to hit enough big plays to keep it within single digits, calling it a game that "just feels like a backdoor cover." Picking the Raiders to win on Sunday is a lonely spot this week. Picking them to keep it respectable is a crowded one. away.headline: Sam Darnold, Drew Lock Injury Updates Provided by Seahawks HC Ahead of Raiders Game
away.blurb: Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold has been ruled out for Week 10 against the Las Vegas Raiders, head coach Mike Macdonald said on Monday. ESPN's Adam Schefter previously reported that "Darnold could attempt to try to return for next Sunday's game in Las Vegas, but the Seahawks also know that they have their bye the following week. By missing the next two games, Darnold could get the chance to rest the next three weeks before the Seahawks play a big divisional Week 12 game in San Francisco against the 49ers." Macdonald clarified it was the quad injury, not the cracked rib, keeping Darnold out of Week 9 action. The Seahawks first listed Lock on the injury report as limited with a right forearm issue ahead of a Week 6 loss at the Denver Broncos. Lock was listed as limited with a right elbow injury the following week before he was ruled out of a Week 7 win over the visiting Kansas City Chiefs. Meanwhile, backup Drew Lock appeared to get good news as looks to recover from an oblique injury suffered on Sunday: Lock went 19-of-28 for 175 yards, one touchdown and zero interceptions in a 17-3 win over the Arizona Cardinals in Week 9. Darnold has been considered week-to-week but won't be placed on IR, according to Macdonald. Darnold cracked a rib on the second play of a Nov. 2 loss to the Chicago Bears before suffering the quad injury late in the game, according to Macdonald. Lock had been previously been dealing with an elbow injury but played this past week with Jalen Milroe backing him up against the Cardinals. Darnold has started seven games for the Seahawks this season, completing 60.2 percent of his passes with 1,478 yards and 10 touchdowns alongside nine interceptions. Lock started in Weeks 2 and 3 after Darnold suffered a glute injury in his team's season opener. He most recently served as the Seahawks' emergency third quarterback against the Bears while Milroe backed up Darnold. Macdonald said after the Oct. 25 game the Seahawks didn't yet know the severity of Lock's injury but that it was "best for us right now to try to calm it down the best we can." Milroe has yet to see game action this season. He took just three snaps across three different contests during his rookie campaign with the Seahawks. The Seahawks (5-4) are currently deadlocked with the Los Angeles Rams for second in the NFC West behind the San Francisco 49ers (7-1).

away.headline: Raiders' Thursday Injury Report Gives Reason for Cautious Optimism
away.blurb: On Wednesday, the official injury report listed defensive tackles Thomas Booker and Folorunso Fatukasi and tight end Ian Thomas as limited participants. Cornerback Darien Porter missed Wednesday's practice with a groin injury he suffered against the Jets. On Thursday, Las Vegas' injury report remained minimal. Porter returned to practice on Thursday, which is good news for the Raiders' young defensive backfield. He was a limited participant, and Thomas was a full participant. Booker did not practice on Thursday. Dont'e Thornton was limited as well. Raiders' Thursday Injury Report Gives Reason for Cautious Optimism Skip to main content SI.COM The Las Vegas Raiders are just a few days away from facing the San Francisco 49ers on the road. Las Vegas went back to work on Thursday, looking to build upon their Week 9 win over the New York Jets. Las Vegas' success this season has largely depended on the quality of the opponent they face. The Raiders have played well enough to beat four of the league's worst teams, but have struggled against the league's elite, which the 49ers are. Still, those four wins are more than the Raiders had all last season, and they are unquestionably better than last season. It may have been against the Jets, but Las Vegas aims to translate its second-half success against New York to this Sunday against the 49ers. After struggling in the third quarter all season, the Raiders' offense exploded against the Jets. In Week 8, Kirk Cousins led the Raiders downfield to score on their first offensive drive after halftime for the first time all season. It was more than impactful, as it led to Las Vegas producing their best third quarter of the season. The Raiders must continue to play well on offense to help their defense. “I think the first play of the second half might have been the throw to Brock [Bowers], and I thought that was a key play in the game and a great call by our coaches, and that whole drive, to finish that drive, it got us right back in the game, which we needed, very important," Cousins said earlier this week. “If you punt and they go down and score, it could be a whole different story. So, it’s very important, and we’ve got to be really strong in the third quarter the rest of the way. And I felt we have continued, last week in the fourth quarter, continuing to play well in the fourth quarter. But it’s a four-quarter game. You’ve got to do it, all four of them.” Throughout the rest of the season, Las Vegas needs the Cousins who showed up in the third and fourth quarters against the Jets to show up in each of their next three games. Moving forward, they will need that version of Cousins and their offense even before the third quarter. Fatukasi was a full participant as well. Based on their injury report, Las Vegas appears to be the healthiest it has been this season, as their Week 1 injury report listed stars Ashton Jeanty and Brock Bowers. The Raiders will likely give rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses a bigger role

San Francisco's two starting outside cornerbacks both exited late in the game and did not return. Renardo Green injured his back while intercepting a pass from Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins in the end zone. Meanwhile, Deommodore Lenoir left the game with a foot injury. Both Green and Lenoir are considered day-to-day, leaving open the possibility that they could be available for the 49ers' Week 10 road matchup against the Dallas Cowboys. Shanahan had previously confirmed that defensive tackle Gracen Halton suffered a broken ankle, ending the promising rookie's season. The coach clarified that Halton sustained a dislocated and fractured ankle, will undergo surgery this week, and will be placed on injured reserve. "I don't think so," the coach said. "I mean, I didn't ask that, but I'd be surprised. But I can ask that later, answer on Wednesday, but I doubt it." Halton wasn't the only 49ers player to get injured against Las Vegas. Shanahan also confirmed that San Francisco plans to open the practice window for defensive tackle C.J. West on Wednesday. West landed on injured reserve after suffering a bone chip in his knee. Unfortunately, wide receiver Mike Evans isn't expected back on the practice field Wednesday. He continues to deal with Achilles tendinitis. "Mike, not expecting him to be ready to go," Shanahan said. "We'll see how he is later in the week, but C.J. and Deebo, expecting to get them back on Wednesday to at least start practicing." This week, it's the wide receiver room that's taken a hit, with Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel Sr. out for another game. Later in the week, Christian Kirk was placed on injured reserve after hurting his meniscus. It's uncertain how serious the injury is, but the 49ers are hoping that it's not too bad when looking at their current situation. Under Kubiak, Las Vegas has beaten the teams they have improved enough to beat. This is, again, more than can be said about recent Raiders teams. Still, the Raiders committed to excellence long ago. away.headline: Cardinals QB situation takes stunning turn with Gardner Minshew update: report
away.blurb: Following their 17-3 road loss Sunday to the Seattle Seahawks, the Arizona Cardinals received a major update on quarterback Gardner Minshew, who may have suffered a season-ending injury. On Monday evening, NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported that Minshew “is feared to have suffered a torn UCL in his throwing arm.” Rapoport said Minshew suffered the injury before halftime but continued playing through it. According to Rapoport, Minshew will get additional testing done, but the injury could end his season and require a lengthy rehabilitation process. Minshew suffered the injury when he was hit by Seahawks pass rusher Dante Fowler while attempting a pass on the final play of the first half. The Cardinals quarterback grabbed his right arm after the rough hit, but continued to play. In Sunday’s game, Minshew completed 21 of 30 passes for 166 yards and was sacked three times by the Seahawks defense. Seattle held Arizona to just 198 total yards of offense for the game. More news: Chiefs HC Andy Reid Reveals Patrick Mahomes Injury Update Ahead of Falcons Game The devastating update arrived days after the team traded veteran starter Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens. Arizona’s unfortunate situation with Minshew has led to several developments, including Adam Schefter reporting that the team signed Josh Johnson off the Cincinnati Bengals’ practice squad. This is Johnson’s 15th team in 14 seasons. According to ESPN , in an initial report on the Cardinals’ injury updates, rookie Carson Beck was expected to start on Sunday. The Cardinals drafted the former Miami Hurricanes quarterback at No. 65 in the 3rd round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Beck led his team to the College Football Playoff National Championship game, which they lost to Fernando Mendoza and the Indiana Hoosiers. The decision to draft Beck was met with mixed reviews, with many sports outlets giving the team a low grade for the pick. NFL.com’s Chad Reuter graded Arizona’s Day 2 picks, including Beck, an “A,” indicating he had “a lot of big-game experience.” However, Reuter also noted that Beck’s decision-making was too inconsistent to be a “surefire starter.” Beck appeared in the NFL Hall of Fame Game this preseason against the Carolina Panthers, throwing for 188 yards and a touchdown in Arizona’s 33-30 loss. With ESPN reporting that Beck is expected to start Sunday, he’s poised to take over for a 3-6 Arizona team, unless they opt to use Johnson instead. Unfortunately, both quarterbacks could face a challenging matchup for the team’s next NFL game. The Cardinals host a Los Angeles Rams team on Sunday, Nov. 15, that has now won three straight games to improve to 5-4 for the season. The Rams also just got back the NFL Defensive Player of the Year, Myles Garrett, who recorded three sacks on Sunday in their 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders, so Beck or Johnson could face a difficult test for his first NFL start. away.headline: Arizona Cardinals face quarterback crisis as Gardner Minshew faces potential season-ending injury
away.blurb: Head coach Mike LaFleur addressed the media on Monday, confirming that Minshew is scheduled for an MRI to determine the full extent of the damage. While the team has not officially ruled the quarterback out for the year, the organization is already preparing for a transition under center. Reports indicate that rookie Carson Beck is the primary candidate to assume the starting responsibilities should Minshew be placed on the sidelines for an extended period. The Arizona Cardinals are confronting a significant roster challenge following reports that starting quarterback Gardner Minshew II has sustained a torn ulnar collateral ligament (UCL) in his throwing arm. The injury, which occurred during Sunday’s game against the Seattle Seahawks, has raised concerns that the 30-year-old signal-caller may be sidelined for the remainder of the season. The incident took place on the final play of the first half when Minshew was struck while being sacked. Despite the severity of the injury, Minshew returned to the field for the third quarter and completed the game. Following the contest, NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported that the quarterback is undergoing further medical evaluations, with initial assessments suggesting a recovery period that could span several months. Transition to Rookie Leadership and Roster Adjustments Beck’s path to the starting lineup was cleared earlier this week when the Cardinals traded veteran Jacoby Brissett, effectively elevating the rookie to the backup position. Although Beck has yet to make his regular-season debut, he saw significant action during the preseason Hall of Fame Game against the Carolina Panthers, where he completed 15 of 19 passes for 188 yards and a touchdown. His development was previously hindered by a rib injury, but his recent promotion has increased his involvement in team practices. To bolster the quarterback room, the Cardinals are reportedly moving to sign veteran Josh Johnson from the Cleveland Browns' practice squad. The addition of Johnson provides the team with necessary depth as they navigate the uncertainty surrounding Minshew’s status and prepare for the upcoming stretch of the season. away.blurb: Gardner Minshew's season may be over. ESPN's Adam Schefter and Josh Weinfuss reported Monday the Arizona Cardinals quarterback may have suffered a torn UCL during the first half of Sunday's loss to the Seattle Seahawks. While he remained in the game, Schefter noted he is now "seeking additional medical opinions to confirm that he likely will need season-ending surgery." Arizona responded by reportedly making a move to bolster its quarterback depth: Minshew had a high completion percentage in Sunday's loss at 21-of-30, but he threw for 166 yards and zero touchdowns while taking three sacks. The offense managed a mere three points in the 17-3 defeat and was unable to take advantage of a solid performance from the Arizona defense against Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Co. ▶️ Full Cardinals-Seahawks Recap 05:47 Arizona already traded Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens after he was benched for Minshew during the team's Week 8 overtime win over the Dallas Cowboys. That means it will likely be Carson Beck time moving forward following the setback to Minshew. Even if Minshew did not suffer the injury, it wouldn't have been surprising if the Cardinals eventually turned to the rookie. After all, Sunday's loss dropped them to 3-6 as the only team in the NFC West under .500. They are not legitimate contenders this season, so seeing what they have in Beck at some point would have made sense so they could further evaluate the quarterback plans for 2027 and beyond. away.headline: Cardinals rookie QB in line to make NFL debut after Gardner Minshew injury
away.blurb: Minshew, who took over the starting job for the Cardinals after Brissett was benched last week, appeared to injure his arm when taking a sack before halftime on Sunday, Nov. 8. He managed to return and played the rest of the game, but reports emerged on Monday, Nov. 9 that he may need season-ending surgery to repair a torn UCL in his throwing arm. Despite the injury, which happened on the last play of the second quarter, the veteran managed to stay in the game after halftime. Minshew played out the rest of his first start of the season, attempting 18 more throws and completing 11 of them in the second half. Rookie quarterback Carson Beck appears set to make his NFL debut in Week 10 after veteran Gardner Minshew sustained a potentially season-ending injury in the Cardinals ' Week 9 loss to the Seattle Seahawks . Beck spent the first eight weeks of the season as the Cardinals' No. 3 quarterback on the depth chart. Arizona's decision to trade Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens on Friday, Nov. 6 moved the rookie to the backup role behind Minshew in Week 9. One week later, a window has opened for Beck to make his first start. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Minshew "is seeking additional medical opinions" before undergoing the procedure. The Cardinals do not have another quarterback on their active roster or on their practice squad. Beck, the Cardinals' third-round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, finished his collegiate career at Miami (Fla.) after spending two seasons as the starting quarterback at Georgia. The former Bulldog led the Hurricanes to an appearance in the CFP National Championship, where they fell to the Indiana Hoosiers and 2026 No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza. Minshew "likely will need season-ending surgery on a torn UCL" in his throwing arm, according to ESPN reporting. The elbow injury, which is much more common in baseball pitchers, is similar to the one that 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy sustained in the NFC championship clash with the Eagles after the 2022 season. The Cardinals' starter seemed to suffer his arm injury at the end of the first half of his team's Week 9 loss to the Seahawks . Edge rusher Dante Fowler managed to get a hand on Minshew's arm as the quarterback began his throwing motion, stripping the ball from Minshew's grip. Minshew immediately grabbed at his right forearm after the contact from Fowler. When the play was over, he rolled on the ground in apparent pain before getting up and running off the field. Further evaluation of Minshew's injury revealed the extent of the injury. Minshew is reportedly seeking alternate opinions before undergoing the season-ending procedure to repair the torn elbow ligament.

home.headline: ‘They Didn’t Have To Tell Us That,’ ‘Definitely Unusual’ — NFL Analyst Questions Seahawks’ Decision To Reveal Sam Darnold’s Surprise Injury
home.blurb: The Seattle Seahawks will be without Sam Darnold for their Week 9 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals, but the timing of the team’s announcement seems questionable to some, especially given its decision to disclose the quarterback’s injuries. “So they got a lot of faith in Drew Lock. I just think that this idea that Wednesday, out of the blue, they tell us that Sam Darnold is out with a quad injury. They tell us that he’s week to week, which usually means you’re going to miss a couple of weeks. They didn’t have to tell us that,” Florio said. “Now I appreciate the transparency, because what they could have done, they could have just put him down as did not practice. They could have done that yesterday. They could have done it today. They could have done it tomorrow, and then they could have called him out on Friday,” the analyst continued. Drew Lock is expected to start against Arizona, although his availability for Seattle is not settled. The veteran is managing a right-elbow injury and was listed as limited on Wednesday’s estimated injury report after Seattle held a walkthrough. Darnold, meanwhile, is considered week-to-week and has not been placed on injured reserve. The cracked rib could potentially be managed while playing, but the quad injury is expected to keep him out against Arizona. Coach Mike Macdonald confirmed Wednesday that Darnold would miss Sunday’s game because of a quad injury suffered late in Seattle’s 34-17 loss to the Chicago Bears. Mike Florio Questions Seahawks’ Decision To Announce Sam Darnold’s Absence Early While the coach disclosed the injury, Macdonald also revealed that the quarterback had played through a cracked rib for nearly the entire game. Darnold suffered the injury on the second play against Chicago after taking a hard hit from blitzing cornerback Kyler Gordon. He did not report the issue to the coaching or medical staff during the game and continued playing through the final whistle. He finished with two touchdown passes despite the injury, and Seattle’s coaches and medical staff did not learn about the cracked rib until after the game. The decision to reveal the extent of Darnold’s injuries, however, prompted NFL analyst Mike Florio to question why Seattle chose to announce the quarterback’s absence on Wednesday rather than wait until later in the week. Speaking on “NFL on NBC” with Chris Simms, Florio said the Seahawks could have followed the league’s injury reporting rules without immediately confirming that Darnold would miss Sunday’s game. “But they decided to just lead with their chin on this, which I thought was strange. It’s definitely unusual, and it forfeits the uncertainty that the Cardinals would have as to who they’re getting ready for. Now they know they’re getting ready for Drew Lock or Jalen Milroe,” Florio added. home.headline: Sam Darnold, Drew Lock Injury Updates Provided by Seahawks HC Ahead of Raiders Game
home.blurb: Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold has been ruled out for Week 10 against the Las Vegas Raiders, head coach Mike Macdonald said on Monday. ESPN's Adam Schefter previously reported that "Darnold could attempt to try to return for next Sunday's game in Las Vegas, but the Seahawks also know that they have their bye the following week. By missing the next two games, Darnold could get the chance to rest the next three weeks before the Seahawks play a big divisional Week 12 game in San Francisco against the 49ers." Macdonald clarified it was the quad injury, not the cracked rib, keeping Darnold out of Week 9 action. The Seahawks first listed Lock on the injury report as limited with a right forearm issue ahead of a Week 6 loss at the Denver Broncos. Lock was listed as limited with a right elbow injury the following week before he was ruled out of a Week 7 win over the visiting Kansas City Chiefs. Meanwhile, backup Drew Lock appeared to get good news as looks to recover from an oblique injury suffered on Sunday: Lock went 19-of-28 for 175 yards, one touchdown and zero interceptions in a 17-3 win over the Arizona Cardinals in Week 9. Darnold has been considered week-to-week but won't be placed on IR, according to Macdonald. Darnold cracked a rib on the second play of a Nov. 2 loss to the Chicago Bears before suffering the quad injury late in the game, according to Macdonald. Lock had been previously been dealing with an elbow injury but played this past week with Jalen Milroe backing him up against the Cardinals. Darnold has started seven games for the Seahawks this season, completing 60.2 percent of his passes with 1,478 yards and 10 touchdowns alongside nine interceptions. Lock started in Weeks 2 and 3 after Darnold suffered a glute injury in his team's season opener. He most recently served as the Seahawks' emergency third quarterback against the Bears while Milroe backed up Darnold. Macdonald said after the Oct. 25 game the Seahawks didn't yet know the severity of Lock's injury but that it was "best for us right now to try to calm it down the best we can." Milroe has yet to see game action this season. He took just three snaps across three different contests during his rookie campaign with the Seahawks. The Seahawks (5-4) are currently deadlocked with the Los Angeles Rams for second in the NFC West behind the San Francisco 49ers (7-1).

That may sound familiar because the Bears will be playing in primetime for the third straight week. That's pretty uncommon. For what it's worth, since 2003, teams playing their third consecutive primetime have gone 16-20 ATS. The past two victories have come against last year's Super Bowl participants with their most recent coming against Seattle with extra time to prepare. This situation is a little trickier since the Bears will be traveling back from Seattle on a short week, which can only be a positive for Tampa. The less time you give Ben Johnson to prepare for an opponent, the better, if you're that opponent. The Bucs have won two straight games in blowout fashion to get right back in the thick of the NFC South race. They've done so despite Baker Mayfield only completing seven total passes, including a grand total of zero last week in a monsoon against Atlanta. The Bucs became the first team since 1974 to win a game without completing a single pass. That does make this handicap a little trickier since we really don't know if his previous thumb injury will be an issue when he has to throw more frequently, which he certainly will need to do tonight. Tampa has ridden its running game, spearheaded by Bucky Irving, and defense during its recent surge. Coming into this week, the Bucs ranked first overall in Defensive DVOA with no glaring holes in their analytical profile. In fact, they actually rank in the top-2 in both drop back and rushing EPA. Todd Bowles has this unit playing at an elite level at the moment, which will create a strength on strength matchup when the Bears have the ball. Chicago Bears Betting Preview There's not much more you can say about the Bears offense at the moment. You could argue it's the best in the NFL with a healthy Caleb Williams , who has seemingly taken a massive leap in the second year of Ben Johnson's offense. He's playing within the structure of the scheme, while also still sprinkling in those off-script explosive plays when things break down. Throw in a dominant ground game and this offense has juggernaut potential. The Chicago defense does have some holes. After all, the Bears are only one of two teams that have allowed six or more yards per play (along with the Raiders ). However, defensive coordinator Dennis Allen does seemingly have a good feel for this group and has been dialing up pressures at all the right times. Plus, this unit should continue to trend up following the addition of Jeffery Simmons and a now healthy Kyler Gordon , who Allen will blitz off the edge to generate some of that aforementioned pressure. It's never going to be an elite defense and there is likely some harsh third-down regression looming on the horizon. Chicago leads the NFL on those late downs by a wide margin at an insane 23.75%. Only one other team in the league has allowed a sub-30% and it's Minnesota at 29.75%. However, as long as Chicago's offense stays heathy and Ben Johnson is on the sidelines, it doesn't need its defense to be elite. Just not a total disaster and this is a true Super Bowl contender. Buccaneers vs Bears Prediction, Betting Analysis I like the Bucs here at +6 or better. I mentioned that potential third-down regression, but I also believe the Bucs will have success on the ground here in a game that might not have a ton of possessions, which makes the road pup a bit more intriguing. I have to imagine it's tough to get up emotionally for three straight primetime games, especially on a short week with travel after beating last year's conference winners. I wouldn't be totally surprised if the Bears were just a tad flat or off in the beginning parts of this game. While I don't think Tampa's defense can completely shut down Chicago's offense, the Buccaneers are playing as well as anybody in the league on that side of the ball at the moment. Even if I adjust for schedule, I have the Bucs rated as a top-3 defense this season — and in order to have a prayer against a Ben Johnson offense, you have to be stout against the run. Tampa has certainly fit that profile for years under Bowles and does so once again this season (second in rush DVOA). I'm selling high on the Bears and taking the six points with Baker and the boys. The Bucs have beaten the Carolina Panthers and Atlanta Falcons , a pair of NFC South rivals, by a combined score of 59-13 in the last two weeks to pull within a half-game of first place in the division. Now they must show they are capable of beating one of the NFL's top teams when they go on the road to take on the 6-2 Chicago Bears on Sunday night. The Bears are on a much different level than either the Panthers or the Falcons, and the Bucs will need to bring their A-game if they want to pull off the upset. If Tampa Bay can earn what would be its signature victory of the season, it will send a message to the rest of the NFC that the Bucs are for real and not to be taken lightly. If the Bucs lose, it will once again cast doubts over what their ceiling is this season. With the NFL's trade deadline coming up on Tuesday, how the Bucs fare against the Bears is likely to have a big impact on the organization's decision to be buyers or sellers. There are several players the Bucs could target at the deadline who could help them make a playoff push. Tampa Bay also has a few veterans who could fetch valuable draft picks if the team decides to sell. Sunday night's clash features the two best rushing offenses in the NFL. The Bucs average over 168 yards per game on the ground, while the Bears average over 150. Chicago leads the league with 17 rushing touchdowns. The first two of my five keys to a Buccaneers' victory are that the Bucs must stay committed to their running game and stop the Bears from running wild. Tampa has the NFL's stingiest rush defense but will have its hands full against the Bears. Last week, Chicago sent two first-round draft picks to the Tennessee Titans for stud defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, who has already taken the defense to a new level. Simmons is a game-changer for the Bears, and his presence will make it much harder for Tampa's offense to find success on the ground. Or through the air. That is, if the Bucs even try to move the ball through the air. Last week, the Bucs became the first NFL team in over 50 years to win a game without completing a pass. The Bears aren't the Falcons. To beat Chicago, Tampa must have a more balanced attack. The Bears' passing offense, on the other hand, is elite. QB Caleb Williams may be the MVP favorite, if not for a three-game absence due to a hamstring injury. The Bears have surrounding Williams with weapons. Luther Burden III and Rome Odunze give Chicago a dynamic WR duo. Colston Loveland is one of the best and most dangerous tight ends in the NFL. Tampa cornerbacks Zyon McCollum and Jacob Parrish have played lights out all season and will once again have to step up against a terrific passing attack. This game will have serious playoff implications for the Bucs and could be the difference in whether the organization buys or sells at the deadline. Marching into Chicago and marching out with a win is a tough task for any team, especially one that seems to have only half an offense like the Bucs. I think the Bucs keep things close all game, but the Bears always seem to be just out of reach throughout. Prediction: Bears 30, Bucs 19

Chicago's high-powered offense and top-tier rushing attack host a 3-5 Buccaneers squad that has won two straight (despite not completing a single pass in their last game) and boasts the NFL's top ground game led by Bucky Irving. The Bears are favored by about six points, but Tampa Bay's physical run defense and Baker Mayfield's ability to keep games close make this a real test before the bye. Several prominent national analysts have pointed to this game as a trap/upset in the making. What follows are our score pick, winner, and projected stat lines for a Sunday Night Football matchup that could push Chicago deeper into the NFC race. Sunday, November 8, 2026 , at Soldier Field . Kickoff: 7:20 p.m. CT (8:20 p.m. ET) Streaming: Peacock and NFL+ (Chicago area) Radio: ESPN Chicago (1000 AM / 100.3 FM HD2) and LATINO MIX 93.5 FM (Spanish) National broadcast team is Mike Tirico (play-by-play), Cris Collinsworth (analyst), and Melissa Stark (sideline). Local Bears radio is Jeff Joniak, Tom Thayer, and Jason McKie. Our Game Scores and Predictions Josh : I think the Bucs get their yards in the air this game, with Chicago's depleted secondary giving up a pair of scores and the run game getting them into field goal range. By contrast, I think Chicago's offense doesn't miss a beat and they hang a pair through the air and a pair on the ground with a Santos field goal to round it out. 31-17 Bears. Jeff Berckes : There's something about what this Bears team is building, where we're at on the schedule, and the narrative that feels like there's an outburst coming. Bucs defense is good, I'm not discounting that – I just think the offensive operation is getting to a level of inevitability. Defense, empowered by the Jeffery Simmons move, want to show out at home. Bears 41 – Bucs 13. Sam : I'm no longer scared of good defenses. But that doesn't make this game a walk in the park. The Bears are due for a letdown. It's a tough spot — three straight primetime games and the bye week looming. I think the Bucs' defense keeps them in the game, but Chicago still gets theirs and Rome Odunze breaks through for a touchdown. The defense is stymied by a good Bucs OL and the run defense struggles. I just can't trust Baker to suddenly wake up the passing game, but I can't rule it out. His thumb has to be healing. Bears still have enough to get it done, but the Bucs cover. Bears 28, Bucs 23 Mongo Peanut : With Tristan Wirfs looking uncertain (he'll play, but he had a DNP and a limited at practice this week with a toe injury) , I think the Bears' new look line piles up the sacks on Baker. The Bears offense keeps humming and wins 37-14. Gary: Bears feed off an energized crowd in Jeffery Simmons' first home game as a Bear; offense continues to do what it's been doing, and that is being dominant. Bucs will get a score before halftime, as per tradition, to make it close at the half, but in the second half the Bears pull away. GOOCH : I can't speak for anyone else, but I'm offended by how many national talking heads are calling this a trap game and suggesting the Bucs defense is going to put Caleb in his place. This Bears team is for real, but so many seem to want to pick it apart, despite all the evidence to the contrary. Well, I'm predicting a signature game for Caleb: 350 yards passing, three touchdown passes, one touchdown run. Rome goes off for 125 yards and a score, Loveland and Burden add their own. Swift puts up over 100 yards on the ground and adds another score. Bears limit the Bucs' rushing attack to its lowest output of the season, and Baker is on the run the whole game. Booker, Sweat, and Simmons all score sacks. Thineman and Malik add interceptions. Final score: 42-3. Take that, national talking heads. Now it's your turn.
