picks.blurb: 3 bold predictions for the Bears against the Buccaneers - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football MNF: Bills-Vikings live updates Week 10 Waiver Wire Jaguars' blockbuster deal Giannis left 'speechless' CFP doubling in size 3 bold predictions for the Bears against the Buccaneers Oct 22, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Chicago Bears wide receiver Rome Odunze (15) | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Casey McAleer · Da Windy City Sun, November 8, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Chicago Bears are 6-2, and they spend Sunday night at home in primetime against a 3-5 Buccaneers. The Bears stand to gain the lead in the NFC North provided they win, and the Minnesota Vikings lose to the Buffalo Bills. That sounds simple enough, but if you've followed this team all season, you know nothing about the Bears is ever simple. As such, here are three bold predictions for Sunday night's game. Luther Burden III goes over 100 yards again Burden put up 130 yards against New England the last time the Bears played in primetime, and he's only taken on more of the offense since then, with 19 catches for 281 yards and two touchdowns in the three games since Caleb Williams returned to the field. Tampa Bay has to commit bodies to stopping the run, because that's what every team has to do against Chicago under Ben Johnson. When that happens, it must open up someone on the outside, and that someone has been Burden. Rome Odunze finally scores a touchdown Odunze has been a good receiver for Williams, posting 28 receptions, 468 yards, and a team best 16.7 yards per catch. But through eight weeks this season, he has still yet to scratch a touchdown. Coach Johnson keeps scheming Odunze open, the chances keep coming, but for whatever reason, it hasn't been in the cards yet. On Sunday night, in front of the national audience, the most due touchdown must finally happen. Jeffery Simmons breaks the ground war The Tampa Bay Buccaneers took the crown as the best rushing team in the NFL from the Bears only last week, after they posted a franchise record of 324 rushing yards against the Atlanta Falcons. The Bears only recently traded two first round picks to go and get Jeffery Simmons from the Tennessee Titans, and he's made an immediate impact. In his Bears debut, Simmons recorded six tackles, a sack, two tackles for loss, and a pass defended. The bold call is two sacks from Simmons, and he'll help to hold the Buccaneers to under 100 rushing yards. If the Bears can hit all three of these bold predictions, they'll be in a very good position to win this game and potentially take first place in their division. But if none of these three things happen, the Bears may just fall into their own trap. | More Bears on DaWindyCity | Riq Woolen comments on potential trade shouldn't change Bears deadline plans Luther Burden III's concussion comes with a single silver lining Austin Booker's ascension should change Bears' trade deadline plans Rome Odunze finally found the end zone Tonight, Bears fans are Bills fans This article was originally published on www.dawindycity.com as 3 bold predictions for the Bears against the Buccaneers .

home.headline: Bucs-Bears Inactives | Emeka Egbuka Returns to Action
home.blurb: WR Emeka Egbuka, who leads the Buccaneers in receptions in 2026, is back in the mix after missing two games with a foot injury, but OLB Yaya Diaby is out due to a knee ailment The Tampa Bay Buccaneers' offense will have one more weapon available on Sunday night when they take on the Chicago Bears, as second-year wide receiver Emeka Egbuka, who was listed as questionable due to a foot injury on Friday's injury report, has been cleared to play. Despite missing the past two games due to that ailment and a concussion, Egbuka leads the Buccaneers with 28 catches and two touchdown receptions. The Buccaneers and Bears submitted their list of inactives at 6:52 p.m. ET on Sunday, 90 minutes before the scheduled kickoff of their Week Nine meeting at Soldier Field. The Buccaneers did not make any practice squad elevations this week and thus have 53 available players on Sunday, meaning they had to name five inactives to get down to the game-day limit of 48. The Bears elevated running back Salvon Ahmed from the practice squad to a roster that had 52 players and therefore had to name five players inactive. The Bears will be without one half of their very effective backfield duo, as running back Kyle Monangai will miss a fifth straight game due to thumb and toe injuries. In addition, rookie cornerback Malik Muhammad is out due to a toe injury but fellow cornerback Tyrique Stevenson, who was a late-week addition to the injury report, has been cleared to play. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Josh Allen and Buffalo's explosive offense face Brian Flores' dominant defense, while Carson Wentz replaces the injured Kyler Murray Imagn Images In the Week 9 edition of "Monday Night Football," the Minnesota Vikings host the Buffalo Bills . Minnesota is coming off its first loss of the season after starting the year with six straight wins. The Vikings turn to Carson Wentz to start in place of Kyler Murray , who is dealing with a hamstring injury. Minnesota sports arguably the NFL's best defense, and it will be put to the test on Monday night against the Bills. Buffalo has won three consecutive games to improve to 6-1, and last week beat up on the Baltimore Ravens following an injury to Lamar Jackson on the Ravens' first snap of the game. Buffalo is in first place in the AFC East behind its efficient and explosive offense, which has helped offset a defense that has been highly vulnerable this year. Will the Vikings bounce back, or will the Bills continue to roll? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. How to watch Vikings vs. Bills live Date: Monday, Nov. 9 | Time: 8:15 p.m. ET Location: U.S. Bank Stadium (Minneapolis) TV: ESPN/ABC | Streaming: Fubo ( try for free ) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bills -3, O/U 43.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Bills have the ball This is going to be one of the most fascinating matchups of the season, as arguably the NFL's best quarterback ( Josh Allen ) will do battle with arguably the NFL's best defensive play-caller (Brian Flores). We know the state of play: the Vikings are going to blitz on damn near every snap, and the Bills are going to have to figure out how in the world to deal with all the extra bodies the Vikings send against both the run and the pass. Last week, the Vikings totally shut down one of the best offenses in the league during the first half, holding the Lions to a mere 154 total yards (on 36 plays, an average of 4.3 per play) and only six points prior to the break. They frustrated Jared Goff and the passing game with their heavy blitzing and they limited Jahmyr Gibbs and company to a 25% rushing success rate. Buffalo has been one of the best running teams in the NFL, averaging 4.8 yards per carry, which ranks fourth in the league. The Bills can lean on James Cook, who, after leading the NFL in rushing last year, is actually averaging nearly six more rushing yards per game than he did a year ago. Buffalo likes to get downhill runs with schemes like duo that create double teams inside, which is tough to do against the Vikings, but can lead to big gains if you can block them up front. Whether the Bills can do that is obviously another question. It's important to note that Allen has been blitzed on exactly a third of his dropbacks, per Tru Media, meaning he's faced the 11th-highest blitz rate in the NFL. He's 46 of 70 for 587 yards, three touchdowns and three interceptions on those plays, and he's been sacked six times. That's all led to him checking in fourth in yards per attempt (8.4) and seventh in passing success rate (50.0%) but only 15th in EPA per dropback thanks to the interceptions. The Bills will need to get the ball out quickly against the blitz, which could mean underneath targets like Khalil Shakir and passing-down back Ty Johnson are heavily involved. It might be a lighter game for the likes of Dalton Kincaid and Dawson Knox , as teams often keep their tight ends back in pass protection against Flores' blitz-happy defense. It might also be tough for DJ Moore and Keon Coleman to get open down the field, but there could be opportunities for big plays if the offensive line does hold up on any given snap. The Vikings have given up the occasional deep shot this year because they send so many men after the quarterback and it leaves them shorthanded on the back end at times. When the Vikings have the ball The Vikings have struggled to move the ball pretty much all season. Their 4.7 yards-per-play average is tied for third-worst in the NFL. Their 1.71 points-per-drive average is fifth-worst in the NFL. And their -0.14 expected points added per play average is second-worst in the NFL, according to Tru Media. They've yet to gain more than 364 yards in any game, and they've been at 275 or fewer in five of their seven contests. They've scored more than 23 points just one time, and it was back in Week 1 when they had touchdown drives of 28, 1 and 14 yards late in the game against the Green Bay Packers . Some of the struggles can be laid at the feet of Kyler Murray, who has completed 64.9% of his passes at an average of just 6.6 yards per attempt, with a mere five touchdown passes and three interceptions. Some of the struggles can be laid at the feet of the run game, where the backs have combined to average south of 4.0 yards per carry. Jordan Mason missed four games, but it's not like he's been effective when he's been on the field, having averaged 3.9 yards a pop. Murray won't be on the field on Monday night. It'll be Carson Wentz under center in his place. Wentz went 23 of 39 for 276 yards and three touchdowns in one-plus games in relief of Murray earlier this year. He seemed to have more command of the offense and more chemistry with Justin Jefferson than Murray does, at the very least. Jefferson went for eight catches for 92 yards and two scores during Wentz's relief appearance back in Week 1, and he was on the receiving end of seven of Wentz's 19 pass attempts in that game. (Wentz's start the following week came in a driving rainstorm in Chicago and doesn't provide much room for analysis.) If the Vikings can keep Wentz well-protected, there should be some opportunities for Jefferson, Jordan Addison and T.J. Hockenson to find openings in what has been a very leaky back seven. The Bills have been solid against the run this year, allowing only 3.9 yards per carry. Given the Vikings' struggles on the ground, it seems unlikely that they'll have much in the way of success running the ball here. You can't ask me to buy into this Minnesota offense right now — not even against Buffalo's leaky defense. We just saw the Vikings put up a relatively limp offensive performance against the Lions. And if there's a team out there that can run the ball on Minnesota the way the Lions did, it might be the Bills with Josh Allen and James Cook. Buffalo can win a low-ish scoring game here by doing just that. away.headline: Bills injury report: Dion Dawkins, Joshua Palmer miss practice again
away.blurb: Starting left tackle Dion Dawkins missed practice for the second straight day Friday because of a rib injury, while right tackle Spencer Brown remained limited with the back injury that kept him out of Sunday's victory over the Baltimore Ravens . Six Buffalo players did not practice Friday, although wide receiver Khalil Shakir was absent for personal reasons and defensive back Sam Franklin Jr. was out with an illness. There was some encouraging news. Tight end Dalton Kincaid returned to full participation after being limited Thursday because of a chest injury, while running back Ty Johnson returned after missing the previous day's practice with an illness. Brown has been limited both days because of a back injury that has bothered him since Buffalo's Week 5 victory over the Los Angeles Rams . The receiver pulled up while running a deep route late in the first quarter. He went to the ground and was ruled out for the remainder of the game. Palmer has already missed time this season because of a shoulder injury that kept him out of Buffalo's Week 5 victory over the Rams. The Bills also listed Keon Coleman as limited for the second consecutive day because of a shoulder injury. D.J. Moore remained limited with the shoulder injury that previously cost him two games. Moore returned against Baltimore but also hyperextended his knee during the fourth quarter. Kincaid was a full participant Friday after being limited Thursday because of a chest injury. The Bills also opened the 21-day practice window for defensive back Jordan Hancock on Thursday. Hancock, who has been on injured reserve since September because of a hamstring injury, remained limited Friday. The Vikings also practiced without wide receiver Jauan Jennings on Friday after he was limited Thursday because of a calf injury. Darrisaw was limited Thursday but returned to full practice Friday. Van Ginkel, who is tied for fifth in the NFL with 6.5 sacks, remained limited with a chest injury. He recorded 2.5 sacks against Detroit on Sunday. Claiborne is currently in his 21-day return-to-practice window.
